chapters.name: The Road from Lanternhold
chapters.brief: Tesfaye says the two of you leave before dawn. He does not say why. Two men in the keep have already tried to make sure you never find out.

chapters.name: The Open Hand
chapters.brief: Tesfaye's letter names an inn and two friends. The road there has wolves, a squire hunting them, and a mage on the steps who knows your face.

enc.label: The steps of the Open Hand

chapters.name: South to Dunmere
chapters.brief: The tainted iron comes from the Dunmere mines. Between here and there: Thornbury, an elf with a grudge, a knife in an inn, and a gnoll fortress with a witch in it.

chapters.name: The Dunmere Mines
chapters.brief: The miners will not go down. Whatever is fouling the ore is four levels below, and it has a priest.

chapters.name: The Bandit Camp
chapters.brief: Grukhar's letters name a courier in Thornbury and a lord of bandits in the Gnashing Wood. Yohannes says go north. He does not say it will be pleasant.

chapters.name: Mirkhollow
chapters.brief: The letters point into the Mirkhollow: spiders, druids who consider you trespass, wyverns, and a mine that is not on any map.

chapters.name: The Iron Mine
chapters.brief: The Consortium's secret mine, worked by slaves under a mage named Olamide. There is a valve at the bottom that can drown all of it.

chapters.name: Varenholm's Gate
chapters.brief: Serpent's Span, the checkpoint, and the city at last. A Burning Gauntlet officer wants something in the sewers dead and a trading house looked at.

chapters.name: The Consortium Tower
chapters.brief: The mine's orders lead to the Iron Consortium's headquarters. Adebayo wants their records. Inside, a well-dressed merchant offers help and asks you to stop his father.

chapters.name: Return to Lanternhold
chapters.brief: The keepers are hearing the dispute over poisoned iron. Take the Consortium's orders to Lanternhold, confront Adigun and his partners, and find out where Kolade has gone.

chapters.name: The Hunted City
chapters.brief: Wanted posters carry your face. Emeka Obi is dead, Segun Marr commands the Gauntlet, and Duke Adebayo is dying under the care of a physician who is not a physician.

chapters.name: The Coronation
chapters.brief: Kolade will be sworn in as Grand Duke tonight and declare war on Calder by morning. You have an invitation, the evidence, and a company in borrowed clothes.

chapters.name: The Undercity
chapters.brief: Under the thieves' maze is an older city, and under that is a temple. Kolade's people are between you and it. So is the one who loves him.

chapters.name: The Temple of Morrak
chapters.brief: Kolade has lost the city and the war he planned. Follow him into Morrak’s temple before he can complete another sacrifice.

departure.caption: Lanternhold, after the last bell. Tesfaye is standing in your doorway with a lamp, dressed for the road.

0.caption: The storehouse. A stranger in a road-cloak is standing between the shelves. He is not one of the keepers.

closing.caption: A man in spiked black plate steps into the torchlight, taller than any man should be. Tesfaye puts himself between the giant and you.

arrival.caption: A village at the edge of the hills, an hour before dawn. Someone small is running up the road behind you.

0.caption: The Shore Road. Two men are sitting on a milestone: one pale and long-haired, laughing at nothing; the other small and sour, watching you.

1.caption: A young man in a white tabard, running down the road towards you with his hand up.

2.caption: The Open Hand Inn. A lean man in a patched coat sits on the steps with a sheet of paper in one hand and a wand in the other.

arrival.caption: The inn door opens. A broad man with a shield on his back, and behind him a woman with grey in her braids and a look that has already counted you.
Delphine — Beau’s wife, a Warden druid and an old friend of your late stepfather, Tesfaye.

0.caption: The road south. An elf in grey steps out of the trees with his hands where you can see them.
The Dunmere inn, first night. A woman at a corner table raises her cup to you.

1.caption: The river crossing below the gnoll fortress. A huge ranger is arguing with a wizard in red. A tiger waits beside the ranger.

closing.caption: The cage in the fortress yard. A woman in a dark robe waits inside it, quite calm.

arrival.caption: Dunmere. The mayor meets you in the square, mopping his face with a handkerchief.

3.caption: The fourth level opens into a chamber with a black altar. A half-orc in a priest's robe stands behind it, and he has been waiting a long time.

arrival.caption: That night you dream of a field of ash, and a throne of black stone standing in it. Tesfaye is beside it, as though he has always been there.

departure.caption: An old man in a grey cloak sits on the stable wall in Thornbury, eating an apple. You have seen him three times this week.

0.caption: Hollister's Inn. A soft man in a merchant's coat has a table to himself and a cup he has not touched.

1.caption: Following the courier’s map north toward the bandit camp, you reach Holloway Vale. A patrol blocks the crossing.
Holloway Vale, on the way to the bandit camp. You come upon a Burning Gauntlet patrol holding a dark-elf priestess at sword-point.

3.caption: The lord's tent. A man in chains, a chest, and an ogre in a mage's coat rising from the cot.

closing.promptText: Gorruk no longer blocks your way. Cal is still chained beside the chest of letters. Get them both out of the tent.

0.caption: The nest: white web thick as sailcloth between the trunks, and a man hanging in it upside down, apparently at his ease.

1.caption: A ring of standing stones in a clearing. A woman in bark and hide steps out of nothing and puts a staff across the path.
An old man is sitting against the nearest stone. He does not get up.

arrival.caption: Delphine, Beau’s wife and Tesfaye’s old friend, sits beside you at the fire.

2.caption: A cage of iron bars at the end of the second level. The dwarf inside has been waiting in the dark long enough to be polite about it.

3.caption: A study cut into the rock, warm and dry, with shelves of ledgers. A man in a good coat does not look up from his writing.

arrival.caption: The throne again, nearer. Figures stand in the ash now, hundreds of them, and every one of them is looking at the chair.

departure.caption: Serpent's Span: a bridge of black stone, a checkpoint, and behind it the towers of Varenholm's Gate. An officer with a burn-scarred jaw is reading your papers.

arrival.caption: The Ducal Palace. A tired man in a red coat sits at a table covered in maps and does not get up.

departure.caption: Inside the Consortium headquarters, a man in a fine merchant's coat draws you aside before the clerk can ask your business. He introduces himself as Sanni.

2.caption: A floor of silk hangings and one desk. The woman behind it has been expecting you, and has poured two cups.

departure.caption: The hill road to Lanternhold. Sanni, the merchant you met at the Consortium headquarters, is waiting at the milestone with a ring in his hand.

1.caption: Before the hearing, you find the three Consortium partners in the great reading room. Maps and shipping records cover their table.

2.caption: Before you can escort the merchants out, Sanni enters and bars the door. Two of his retainers seize Bankole and Rotimi. Sanni draws a knife and steps toward Adigun.
Sanni drives the knife into Adigun. Behind him, his retainers cut the other two merchants' throats. Sanni wipes the blade inside his sleeve and opens the door.
Sanni calls the keep's guards into the reading room. He points at your company, standing beside the three bodies. His retainers step aside to let the guards through.
The lock turns behind your company. Your weapons are taken to a chest outside the cell. Hours later, Dawit comes to the bars with Tesfaye's sealed letter.
You read it twice. Then you read the last line a third time.
On the back of the letter, Tesfaye has added a warning for both of you.
Dawit opens the cell. You reclaim your gear while he uncovers a narrow passage behind the wall. Footsteps are already coming down the stairs.

arrival.caption: Back at the Consortium tower, away from your company: Sanni has set aside his merchant's coat. He wears the spiked black armour from the Griffon Road. His tutor calls him Kolade.
The throne is close enough to touch. A man in black armour is already sitting in it, and he is smiling at you like a brother.

departure.caption: The Gate, at dawn. Your face is nailed to every post on the street.

1.caption: The Duke's sick-room. A man in a physician's coat stands between you and the bed with a cup in his hand.

2.caption: The docks, at dusk. A woman with two swords across her back is waiting at the end of the pier, alone.

departure.caption: The palace steps, at night. Every window is lit.

0.caption: The great hall. Halfway through the oath, the guests nearest the dukes draw knives.

1.caption: The armoured giant from the Griffon Road pulls off the face of a Grand Duke's guest. Under it is a man who looks like you.

2.caption: A ring of frost. He and his tutor are gone. The rear-guard is not.

1.caption: The gate of the Undercity: an arch of old stone under the thieves' maze. Amara stands in it with both swords drawn.

2.caption: A buried street, lit by torches that should have gone out a thousand years ago.

4.caption: The temple steps. A Gauntlet officer in a new cloak stands at the top with the men he sold.

departure.caption: The Temple of Morrak. The stairs end in a hall of black stone, and the braziers are lit.

2.caption: Kolade waits beside the altar. His helmet lies on the steps. The last of his guards bar the doors behind you.

closing.caption: Kolade falls. His binding breaks, and Hiwot’s soul is free. The throne remains empty.

options.text: Why tonight? What has happened?
You have never been afraid of anything. You are afraid now.
I will get my things.
No one. The same faces as every day.
A pilgrim at the well asked my name. I told him.
Why? Who would come here?
Who paid you? Say the name and I let you walk.
Richer for whom?
You have picked the wrong storehouse.
Go. Run, and I will not follow.
No name. He said there is only ever a seal on a letter and a purse at an inn.
Two hundred in gold for me, alive or otherwise. He wondered why.
I did not ask. There was no time.
Me. Tesfaye said no. We do what he told us — the Open Hand. Stay close to me.
Later. Keep your voice down; grief will not help us, and it will get us found.
He asked whether I knew what I am. I will find him, ask him what he meant, and take him apart.
An inn called the Open Hand. Friends of my father's. He is dead.
South. Family.
That is my business.
Who are you, really? Nobody walks this road for the pleasure of it.
Your friend is laughing at nothing. Is he well?
Four is better than two. Walk with us.
We travel alone. Good road to you.
The Dawning Flame. What is that?
Then we clear them together, and you may tell your Order whatever you like.
A knight who cannot manage wolves. What do they teach in that Order?
We are in a hurry. Manage your own wolves.
Whose name is on that paper? Who is paying?
How did you know to wait here?
You should have stayed home, Merle.
Delphine! Beau! There is a man on your steps who means murder!
A man in black plate, taller than a man should be. He asked for me by name. Tesfaye said no.
Quickly. He did not suffer.
I cannot. Not tonight.
What are the Wardens? He never told me.
Why would a trading house pay two hundred in gold for a scholar's foundling?
He trusted you. So will I. Tell me what he would have done.
I did not come for bread. Tell me who killed him and I will go alone.
Gorruk. Does he use a seal? An iron hand in red wax?
Your wife. I am sorry. What was her name?
Walk with us. When we find him, he is yours.
I have enough grief in this company. I do not need yours.
Why do you do this work?
Then let it be personal.
Why would a Crimson Wizard care what happens to one witch?
We are freeing her. Bahadır, with me.
A hundred gold, and your staff until the Gate. Done.
The witch lives, and the wizard walks with us and holds his tongue about it.
The warleader's throat. I gave it that.
I felt nothing. I fought, and it ended.
You tell me. What is it? Say it plainly.
Whatever you felt, keep it to yourself in front of the others.
What did your crews see, before they stopped going down?
Who profits when your iron goes bad?
We will go down. Two hundred in gold, and the town's thanks.
We will go down. Pay what the town can spare.
Who lied to you? Say the names.
Why foul the ore at all? Who profits from a town starving?
Leave the letters on the altar and walk. Now, before I change my mind.
I will take the letters off your body.
You knew what I was when you brought me to Lanternhold?
I do not want whatever this is. Starve it.
Show me the throne.
"Give the child to me and you may keep your life and your library."
I did not hear it. I was running, as I was told.
Ask him yourself, old man. I am going to.
Why did Tesfaye die? You know. Say it.
The man in black armour. Who is he?
Then help. Not riddles — help.
North, then. Stay out of my way, old man.
A priest under Dunmere had your letters. Your name, your inn, your hand.
Wrong answer.
Fifty in gold for the camp's location. Then you leave this town tonight.
Hiwot. His coat.
What are you fleeing?
Let her go. She is under my protection.
This is not my fight. We keep moving.
There is a bounty? Then I will take her in myself.
Get us invited.
Hiwot. The back gate.
Loud. The front gate, now.
Yes. Take it.
Hold. I want him alive to answer questions.
Break Cal’s chains first. Then take the chest.

reply.caption: You break Cal’s chains, then recover the chest. He can barely stand; you will escort him back to the Wardens. First, he shows you what is in the letters.

options.text: Secure the chest first. Then break Cal’s chains.

reply.caption: You secure the chest, then break Cal’s chains. He can barely stand; you will escort him back to the Wardens. First, he shows you what is in the letters.

options.text: Who pays a bounty on a wyvern?
Wardens cut for nothing. I am not a Warden. What is your debt worth?
Hold still. I’ll cut you free. You can ride with us.
Spiders have to eat too.
What has been done to this wood?
We are here for the men who poison your river with their mine. Your enemy is ours.
Move, or be moved.
What did he write?
He wrote to me about you, too. Not twenty letters. But enough.
You should sleep. It is a long walk to the mine.
Beau is a fortunate man.
We are with you. Everyone comes out.
The mage first. Then the slaves, if there is time.
Paper and knives? How does a trading house take a dwarven mine?
The old ones are dead. Get up; you are with us.
Stay where you are. We will come back for you.
Who do you answer to? Say the name and I may let you keep your ledgers.
Enough. We’re freeing the prisoners.
Turn the wheel. Now.
No one touches that wheel until Beau is up. Hold this room.
Who are the people you answer to?
Copy them tonight. The originals go to the city.
No. And if either of you touches them, you leave this company.
Others. How many? Who?
I will stop him. I will not claim Morrak's throne.
If there are others, I had better be the strongest.
Nineteen. I counted them out.
Cages of them. I did not count.
That is between me and the Duke.
Why does the Duke want me? He does not know me.
Consider it done.
The Gauntlet pays for this, I assume.
Kaito. Talk.
Hiwot. Quietly.
Winston. Pay him.
We go through him.
My company, and now you.
The Umbral Hand has copies. I allowed it.
Wardens. Delphine of the Open Hand read them first.
Then we will get them. For the city.
For the city, and for a price.
The Consortium has been trying to kill me since Lanternhold. Why me, Duke?
We are the company from the south. Olamide sent for us before the mine flooded.
Guards first. The clerk if he runs.
Hiwot, go and see what is on that list.
His life and his library, in exchange for me.
Nothing. He simply took.
Tell me what you are selling first, and I will decide what it costs.
Kolade Adeyinka. Who is he to this city? Say it as if I had never heard the name.
Talk. Quickly.
You will talk to Duke Adebayo. In chains.
You share his bed. You share his end.
If it was Tesfaye's, I want it back.
Keep it. I have not decided whether to trust you.
If this is a trick, I will find you.
The Griffon Road, the night we left. He stood between me and the man who killed him.
Write "on the road." It is all you need.
You paid for the mines and the bandits. You will not leave this room alive.
I will not kill you. Tell me what your son has been doing.
You will answer to Adebayo. All three of you. Nobody dies in a library.
That he had been proud of me every day since he carried me through the gate.
Only "run." And two names.
I did not hear. I was doing as I was told.
He raised a monster and loved it anyway.
Twenty years and he never said a word. He should have told me.
A throne. And a brother sitting in my seat.
Wrong voice. Strike first.
Wrong voice. Strike first.
What did I steal from the brothers' kitchen when I was nine?
...Come here, then. Slowly.
Starve it. I will stop him as myself.
If it takes a god to stop a god, then feed it.
We find Adebayo and we save him. We do this lawfully.
Folake. Kolade's head for her Consortium. I can live with that.
The thieves. A debt is cheaper than a Duke.
Yes.
I loved a man who lied to me for twenty years. Does that count?
No. And I do not intend to start.
How does one stop a man like that without killing him?
If it can be done without killing him, I will do it that way. You have my word.
He killed Tesfaye. He dies.
Of course. You have my word.
Olumide first. He is the one with the sword.
Folasade first. She is the one who will believe us.
Neither. Kolade. Now, while he is on the dais.
Olamide's ledgers. Adigun's confession. Folake's letters. Every duke here can read.
You killed the only father either of us ever had.
You are sitting in my seat, brother.
Lead.
No time. Straight through.
Then draw.
Stand aside. I keep my promises.
Come with us. Help me stop him the way you want him stopped.
Stand aside. He will live.
Never. Not once. He did not know you existed.
Only in a letter, after he was dead. He called you my brother.
There was nothing to say about you. There still is not.
Tesfaye chose me. He would have chosen you too, if you had let him.
Brother. I am sorry for what they did to you. I am still going to stop you.
Get out of my chair.
Nobody sits in it. Starting with you.
You go up those stairs in chains. Amara asked. I promised.
I sit in it. Move.
Sit in it, then. Alone. I am going home.
You murdered Tesfaye, you bastard. I came here to kill you.
You have killed enough people. Surrender.
Before this ends, you are going to tell me the truth.
You ordered these murders. Fighting your men does not make me your accomplice.
I made choices I regret. I am still going to stop you.
I spared people you would have killed. You know that.
How did you learn who your father was?
What happened when Tesfaye found us?
Tell me about Adigun and your plans for the throne.
Enough. I will stop you.
Tesfaye believed you were dead. He did not choose to abandon you.
There is something else I want to know.
What did Adigun know about your plans?
You arranged Adigun’s death and my arrest.
You have lost the war. How can you still ascend?
There is something else I want to know.
Tesfaye should be here. You took him from me. Draw your weapon.
I will stop you. Surrender while you still can.
I know what taking your power would mean. I want it anyway.
Come home, Hiwot. I give up the divine power.
I will keep the power and claim the throne. [Hiwot cannot return.]

q1_wake.t: [low, urgent] Wake, my child, and dress. Not the library robe — the travelling coat, and your boots. We leave Lanternhold tonight.

[calm] I know you have questions. I have dreaded them for twenty years, and I will answer every one once we are past the gate and out of the hearing of these walls. Not before. Trust me in this as you have trusted me in everything.

q1_wake_why.t: [quietly] A message came at dusk, of the kind that is not written down. It said that people who wish you harm know where you are. Lanternhold, which I chose because nothing here changes and no one ever comes, has stopped being safe. That is all I will say inside these walls.

q1_wake_afraid.t: [a breath] Yes. I am afraid. I have never lied to you and I will not begin tonight. Fear is not shameful, my child; it is a messenger. Mine says to have you on the road before the moon is up.

q1_wake_ask.t: [careful] One thing before you go, and answer it truly. Has anyone spoken to you today whom you did not know? A pilgrim, a pedlar, a man asking directions. Anyone.

q1_seen_nobody.t: [relieved] Then they are not inside the walls yet, and we have the hours I hoped for. Take what coin you have to Dawit at the storehouse and buy a true blade; the practice swords stay behind. Meet me at the gate at the second bell, and if anyone stops you between here and there — anyone — do not argue with them. Come to me.

q1_seen_pilgrim.t: [very quiet] You told him. — No. It is not your fault; you had no reason not to. It means they are inside already, and it means we go now, not at the bell. Take your coin to Dawit at the storehouse and buy a true blade, and come straight back to me. Do not stop for anyone.

q1_seen_why.t: [gently] Because the people I have feared for twenty years have found the one place I hoped they never would. That is the whole answer, and I will give you the rest on the road. Take your coin to Dawit at the storehouse and buy a true blade. Then the gate, at the second bell.

q1_cobb.t: [hard] Two of them, inside the keep, on the same night. Somebody bought a keeper's silence for that, and I mean to know whose. Later.
[urgent] The one in the storehouse. Did he say anything before it ended? Who sent him — a name, a house, a mark?

q1_cobb_spared.t: [thoughtful] He went. That was kinder than I would have been in your place. Remember that it cost us nothing tonight; it will not always.
[urgent] And here is a second one, in the brothers' quarters. Before you finish him — the first one. Did he say who sent him? A name, a house, a mark?

q1_cobb_seal.t: [grim] A seal. Then it is a house that wants you, not a man, and houses keep ledgers and ledgers keep names. That is the first useful thing anyone has told me in twenty years. Finish this one; we go the moment the gate opens.

q1_cobb_bounty.t: [quiet] Two hundred. That is not a grudge; that is a budget. Somebody with money has decided you are worth it, and I would give a great deal to know how they came to that sum. Finish this one; we go the moment the gate opens.

q1_cobb_nothing.t: [gently] No. There would not have been. It is a thing you learn: ask first, strike after, when you can. Finish this one; we go the moment the gate opens.

q1_road.t: [quiet] Stay close, and keep to the shadow of the trees. This road is empty at night, and I have learned to dislike empty roads.

[after a silence] {target}. In case I do not find a better moment — I have been proud of you every day since I carried you through that gate. Whatever you hear about yourself in the days to come, hold to that. A tree with deep roots laughs at the wind.
[sharp] Torches. Ahead, and closing. Off the road — now.

q1_refuse.t: [steady] You know my name; I do not know yours, and I find I do not care to. You will not have this child while I stand. Take that as my answer.

q1_answer.t: [level] It knows what I taught it. Letters, kindness, and how to hold a blade. That is all the knowing it needs, and more than you were ever given.
[to the ward, fierce and low] Run. Do not look back, whatever you hear. Find the Open Hand Inn on the Shore Road. Ask for Beau and Delphine. Run!

q4_dream.t: [echoing] You are dreaming, my child, and I am dead, and both of those things are true at once.
[gentle] That throne belonged to Morrak, the god of murder. He died before you were born. You are one of his children, and part of his power lives in you.
[grave] He intended his children to kill one another and take that power for themselves, until one could claim his throne. You can refuse, my child. You do not have to kill for him.

q4_dream_ask.t: [sorrowful] I did. I brought you there to keep you out of Morrak's followers' reach. I should have told you while I was alive. I was afraid of what it would do to you.

q4_dream_reject.t: [warm] Good. That is the harder road, and the right one. You will wake with a gift for closing wounds. Spend it on other people.

q4_dream_embrace.t: [grieving] I cannot stop you here; only you can. You will wake with a gift for opening wounds. Mind what it makes you want.

q7_dream.t: [echoing] The throne is closer this time, my child. You'll keep seeing it as your power grows.

[grave] Morrak, the god of murder, left many children. You are one of them. Some of your kin have begun killing the others for his power. The man who hunts you is using the Consortium's money and hired killers to find them.
[fading] Each child he kills makes him stronger and removes another rival for the throne. That is why he wants you dead. You can stop him without claiming Morrak's throne yourself.

q7_dream_others.t: [quiet] I do not know how many are still alive. Most were raised by mortal families, as you were. Some may not know what they are. The man in black has been searching for them for years.

q7_dream_reject.t: [proud] Twice now. It grows harder each time and you keep saying no. That is what courage is. No one warns you that it is dull.

q7_dream_embrace.t: [grieving] The strongest of them is waiting for you at the end of this road, and he thinks exactly that.
[fading] Please, my child. Be careful what you become on the way to him.

q10_letter.t: [echoing, read aloud] "If you are reading this, my child, I failed to tell you myself, and I am sorry. Your mother was one of many. Your father was Morrak, the god of murder, in the last year before he died — and he sired children so that one of them might one day take his place. You are one. So is the man who killed me. He is your brother. He believes the throne is his. It is not, unless you decide it is."

q10_double.t: [Tesfaye's voice, wrong] {target}. I am not dead. It was a trick — a Warden trick — come to me, child, come here —

q10_dream.t: [echoing] Now you have my letter. I should have told you about your brother myself, when I could still help you face him.

[grave] Kolade plans to murder the other children and take their power. His tutor means to use the deaths in the war as an offering to Morrak, to make Kolade a god. Stop the war and you deny him that sacrifice.
[fading] The last time I ask. Feed it, or starve it.

q10_dream_reject.t: [at peace] Then I did enough. Go and finish it, my child, and come home to whoever is waiting.

q10_dream_embrace.t: [quiet] Then I hope I am wrong about what that costs. I have been wrong before. Not about this. Go.

q10_blood_of_two.t: [echoing] "There is something else I should have told you both. Hiwot is also Morrak’s child. A Warden brought her to Lanternhold after the same raid. I raised you together because neither of you should have had to face this alone.
[echoing] If one of you dies, the power in your blood returns to Morrak’s realm. His priests know how to bind a soul to it. Keep each other away from their altars."

endcard_ending_hero.t: Kolade Adeyinka died beneath the city. The Council made the Consortium's ledgers public and rejected war with Calder. The people of Varenholm knew you had stopped the conspiracy. Few knew that the man you defeated was your brother.

endcard_ending_monster.t: Kolade Adeyinka died at the altar. The Council exposed the Consortium's conspiracy and halted preparations for war. The city celebrated your victory. It knew nothing of Morrak's children, or of the power that had drawn both you and Kolade to the throne.

endcard_ending_usurper.t: You claimed the throne beneath the city after defeating Kolade. The Council halted preparations for war and honored you for exposing the conspiracy. Most of the people who cheered had no idea what you had taken for yourself.

endcard_ending_mercy.t: Kolade Adeyinka was imprisoned beneath the Gauntlet's hall. The Consortium's ledgers were made public, and the Council rejected war with Calder. You had stopped him without killing him. He would face trial for the people he had ordered murdered.

endcard_ending_ascetic.t: You refused the throne and left Kolade alive beneath the city. By dawn, he had disappeared. You returned home, knowing that he might yet come after you. What became of him remained unknown.

endcard_ending_restored.t: Kolade died in Morrak's realm. You released the souls he had bound and gave up the divine power in your blood to bring Hiwot back. She woke beside you on the temple floor, alive and mortal. The passage closed behind you. You had lost your claim to the throne, but you could take your sister home.

endcard_ending_ascended.t: Kolade died in Morrak's realm, and you claimed the power he had tried to take. Hiwot could not return with you. Her soul passed beyond your reach as you became Morrak's successor. You could still walk the mortal world, but you would return to it without your sister.

endcard_allegiance_gauntlet.t: Duke Adebayo recovered and kept his promise to you. The wanted posters came down, and the Gauntlet publicly cleared your company's name. Its hall recorded your part in exposing Kolade.

endcard_allegiance_consortium.t: Folake took control of the Consortium and honored her bargain with you. She began reopening trade routes and hiring new guards. Her letters made it clear that she hoped to employ you again.

endcard_allegiance_thieves.t: Tunde Softfoot had given you a way into the palace when you needed one. Afterwards, he reminded you that the favor had not been a gift. He had yet to name his price.

endcard_allegiance_none.t: The Council publicly cleared your name and thanked you for exposing the conspiracy. You left without entering the service of any of the city's factions.

endcard_dukes_both.t: Olumide and Folasade survived the attack on the Council. Together, they began restoring order and investigating the officials Kolade had paid.

endcard_dukes_one.t: Folasade was buried with the city's honors. Olumide survived, but the attack left the Council badly weakened.

endcard_dukes_none.t: Olumide and Folasade were buried on the same morning. Their deaths left the surviving councillors to choose new leaders and settle a frightened city.

endcard_companion_wren_ward_present.t: Hiwot opened a small locksmith's shop on the harbour road. She repaired locks by day and declined to explain where she had learned to open the difficult ones.

endcard_companion_wren_ward_gone.t: Hiwot returned to Lanternhold. Brother Yonas listened to her account of the journey, then asked her to write it down for the archives.

endcard_companion_dorran_present.t: Beau helped the people driven from their homes by the fighting. When there was heavy work to do, he was usually the first to volunteer. He never had much patience for being called a hero.

endcard_companion_dorran_dead.t: Beau's companions raised a memorial for him near Mirkhollow. They remembered his loyalty, his patience, and how readily he had put himself in danger for others.

endcard_companion_selene_present.t: Delphine helped rebuild the Warden house on the Shore Road. She kept Tesfaye's letters there, along with a room you could use whenever you visited.

endcard_companion_selene_gone.t: Delphine returned to the Wardens. News of the campaign reached her through their reports.

endcard_companion_vess_present.t: Desmond stayed in Varenholm and found work trading information. He was careful about who knew his clients' names.

endcard_companion_vess_gone.t: No reliable news of Desmond reached you after Kolade's defeat. The Umbral Hand refused to discuss its agents.

endcard_companion_fennick_present.t: Winston took work guarding merchant caravans. He insisted on seeing the route, the cargo and the full payment before agreeing to leave town.

endcard_companion_fennick_gone.t: No further word of Winston reached you after Kolade's defeat.

endcard_companion_cassian_present.t: Santiago was knighted by the Order of the Dawning Flame. His report named the companions who had helped him, including those his superiors would rather have left out.

endcard_companion_cassian_gone.t: Santiago returned to the Order of the Dawning Flame. He sent occasional letters, keeping his account of the journey brief.

endcard_companion_ithrel_present.t: Itsuki visited his wife's grave before settling outside the city. He began taking work as a guide again, and made plans that had nothing to do with revenge.

endcard_companion_ithrel_gone.t: Itsuki travelled north after leaving the company. Little news of him reached Varenholm.

endcard_companion_bramm_present.t: Bahadır settled by the river with Fındık. The tiger liked to sleep across the front steps. Visitors soon learned to call from the gate.

endcard_companion_ysolde_present.t: Yasemin stayed in Varenholm to continue her studies. She kept in touch with the people who had helped free her.

endcard_companion_aurelius_present.t: Devendra returned to Vashk and secured a promotion from the Crimson Wizards. He sent you a copy of his report. Your name appeared in it, though not nearly as often as his.

endcard_companion_ilvara_present.t: Layla opened a small chapel in Varenholm. People who would once have crossed the street to avoid her began coming to her for healing. She made them wait their turn like everyone else.

endcard_companion_ilvara_gone.t: Layla left Varenholm after the fighting ended. She gave no destination and made no promise to return.

endcard_companion_faelen_present.t: Kaito found steady work as a tracker. Between jobs, he performed in the inns. He asked you not to mention the spiders during his songs about the campaign.

endcard_companion_faelen_gone.t: Kaito returned to the inns of Thornbury. His songs about the campaign gave him a considerably larger role than you remembered.

endcard_companion_nettle_present.t: Wanjiru returned to Mirkhollow to help restore the riverbanks and woodland damaged by the mine. She had little interest in the celebrations in Varenholm; she wanted to see the river run clear again.

endcard_companion_nettle_gone.t: Wanjiru returned to Mirkhollow after leaving your company. She sent word that the river was beginning to clear.

endcard_companion_durnik_present.t: Dai Morgan obtained permission to reclaim his clan's mine. Before work began, he made copies of the prisoners' names and arranged a memorial for those who had died there.

endcard_companion_durnik_gone.t: Dai Morgan left the company to seek help reclaiming his clan's mine.

endcard_companion_amara_present.t: Amara visited Kolade in prison. She still cared for him, but no longer excused what he had done.

endcard_companion_amara_gone.t: Amara left Varenholm by sea. She asked for privacy and gave no address where she could be reached.

endcard_companion_amara_dead.t: Amara was buried near the entrance to the Undercity, where she had tried to stop you from reaching Kolade.

endcard_romance_cassian_line.t: Santiago asked you to attend his knighting. You went together, then slipped away for supper before the speeches had finished.

endcard_romance_cassian_favoured.t: He asked to help rebuild the damaged streets. You spent several mornings working beside him.

endcard_romance_ithrel_line.t: You and Itsuki make time to walk outside the city. Some days he speaks about his wife. On others, you plan where to travel next.

endcard_romance_ithrel_favoured.t: After the hunt was over, he asked you to visit the woods where he once worked as a guide.

endcard_romance_ilvara_line.t: Layla invites you to her chapel after the day's work. You share meals, argue over the wine, and make plans together.

endcard_romance_ilvara_favoured.t: She insists on keeping her own duties. The two of you arrange time together around them.

endcard_romance_faelen_line.t: Kaito takes you to the inns where he once played for his supper. He remembers the songs better than he claims.

endcard_romance_faelen_favoured.t: His work with the Undervault keeps him busy, but he always makes time for an evening with you.

endcard_romance_amara_line.t: You and Amara agree to take your relationship slowly. There is much still to discuss, including her feelings for Kolade.

endcard_romance_amara_favoured.t: She thanks you for hearing her out. Neither of you pretends that the road ahead will be easy.

endcard_heritage_reject.t: The dreams of Morrak's throne ceased. You had refused his succession and meant to keep that promise.

endcard_heritage_neutral.t: The dreams of Morrak's realm became less frequent, but they did not stop. You still had to decide what your heritage would mean for the rest of your life.

endcard_heritage_embrace.t: The dreams continued, and you welcomed them. You still wanted to know how much of Morrak's power you could claim.

endcard_outcome_beaudrowned.t: Beau and nineteen prisoners died when the mine flooded. Their names were carved into a memorial above the sealed entrance.

endcard_outcome_daiabandoned.t: Dai Morgan was never rescued from the mine. No one could confirm that he had escaped before it flooded.

endcard_outcome_laylasold.t: The patrol took Layla toward the coast in chains. After that, you heard nothing certain about her fate.

endcard_outcome_kaitoabandoned.t: You left Kaito trapped in the spiders' web. After the campaign, no word reached you of whether he had escaped.

endcard_finale_amaramourning.t: Amara mourns Kolade. She had hoped to bring him back alive. She asks for time before speaking about what happened in the temple.

endcard_finale_cityaftermath.t: In Varenholm, the Consortium's ledgers were made public. The Council rejected war with Calder. Caravans began using the roads again, and iron returned to the markets. The families who had lost people to the mines and the hired killers were still waiting for justice.

endcard_finale_amarawaiting.t: Amara stayed in Varenholm for a time, hoping for news of Kolade. She would not say what she would do if he returned.

endcard_heading_hero.t: The Gate Stands. You stopped Kolade and prevented the war.

endcard_heading_monster.t: A Dangerous Inheritance. Kolade is dead. Morrak's power remains within you.

endcard_heading_usurper.t: The Throne Claimed. You defeated Kolade and took the throne for yourself.

endcard_heading_mercy.t: Kolade in Chains. You brought him back alive to answer for his crimes.

endcard_heading_ascetic.t: An Unfinished Reckoning. You refused the throne and left Kolade alive.

endcard_heading_restored.t: Home Together. You gave up the throne to bring Hiwot home.

endcard_heading_ascended.t: Morrak’s Successor. You claimed the throne. Hiwot did not return.

q1_store.t: [easy] Evening. You'd be the old man's ward, then. Younger than I was told, and about to make somebody a good deal richer.
[almost kindly] No call to make this hard. I've a purse to earn and a road to be on before sun-up, and you've got — what, a practice sword? Stand still and I'll make it quick.

q1_nib_who.t: [a shrug] There's never a name, friend. A seal on a letter, a purse left at an inn, a description of a face. That's how it's done, and it's done that way so men like me can't answer questions like yours.

q1_nib_richer.t: [amused] For somebody who don't want to be spoken of. Two hundred in gold for the ward of Tesfaye of Lanternhold, alive or otherwise. That's a heap of money for a scholar's foundling, and I'll be honest, I did wonder why.

q1_nib_run.t: [backing away] ...You're either real kind or real foolish, and I ain't paid enough to find out which.

q1_appear.t: [calm, courteous] Tesfaye of Lanternhold. You have run a very long way to end up on a road at night with the one thing I want.
[measured] Give the child to me, and you may keep your life and your library. It is not a small thing I offer. I will not offer it twice.

q1_question.t: [curious, unhurried] Before you die for it, old man, satisfy me on one point. Does the child know? Have you told it what it is, or have you let it grow up believing it is yours?

q1_after.t: [unhurried, to the dark] Then it will learn the rest from me. Let the child run. The road is long, my friends, and I own most of it.

q10_unmasked.t: [calm] Of course. Adigun wanted frightened customers paying twice the price. He would never have let the armies march. Now the Consortium is mine, and the ward will be hunted as a murderer.
[pleased] Let them run. We know where to look for the other children. Once the war begins, nobody will spare soldiers to protect them. I will deal with Tesfaye's ward when I choose.

q12_reveal.t: [calm, pleasant, to the hall] Enough. Put it down, all of you; nobody in this room is going to be paid tonight, and I would rather not lose good people to bad timing.

[warm, to you] There you are. I have wanted to hear my brother's voice — my sister's — for a year, and I have only ever had it second-hand, from frightened men. Say something. The hall can wait; it is mostly dead.

q12_face_evidence.t: [delighted] Paper! Tesfaye's child brings paper to a coronation. That is the most charming thing I have seen in a year, and I mean that; he taught you well.
[gently] It does not matter. Look at their faces: the war is already in their mouths, and paper does not take words back out. Baba — take me down.

q12_face_aldric.t: [quiet, honest] He was never mine. He chose you. He could have chosen both of us, and he chose you, and I have made my peace with it in a way I do not think you have.

q12_face_throne.t: [a slow, real smile] THERE you are. I knew it. I said to Amara, I said, it will be in the child too, wait and see.
[warm] Come and take it, then. Not here — this is a hall for merchants. Come to the altar and take it from me properly. Baba — take me down.

q14_altar.t: [warm] You came. I hoped you would. Every other one of us I have found, I have had to hunt; you walked here on your own feet, and I find I am proud of that, which is a strange thing to feel about someone I mean to kill.
[calm] Sit with me a moment. Did Tesfaye ever speak of me? In all those years he raised you, did he mention my name? I've waited thirty years to hear that he remembered me.

q14_spoke_never.t: [a long quiet] Not once. — Thank you. I would rather that than a lie, and you could have lied; I would have believed you. It is easier, somehow. A man cannot be refused by someone who never knew he was at the door.

q14_spoke_letter.t: [very still] "Brother." In his own hand. — He could have written it to me. He knew where I was; he made a point of never coming. I have wondered for thirty years what he would call me, and it turns out he called me the right thing and sent it to you.
[gently] Thank you. That was not a kindness, but it was the truth, and I have had little enough of either.

q14_spoke_nothing.t: [laughing softly] Oh, that is his. That is his exactly; he could put a whole man in a sentence and leave the sentence out. — Good. Then we understand each other, and I do not have to be gentle.

q14_plea_answer.t: [gently] Amara. My love. Get up; you are kneeling in ash.

q14_altar_last.t: [patient] Now. Say what you came to say. I have waited thirty years to hear it, and I would like to hear it properly, before we begin.

q14_last_aldric.t: [flinching, then smooth] He did not know me. He had a choice between two children in a gutter and he took the one that cried less; I have never held it against him. I hold it against the gutter.

q14_last_brother.t: [very quiet] Sorry. Nobody has said that to me in thirty years, and you say it as if it cost nothing.
[rising] It changes nothing. Draw, brother. Sister. Blood.

q14_last_throne.t: [laughing] YES. Yes. Come and take it. Whichever of us stands up from this floor gets to be a god, and I would honestly be content either way.

q14_beaten.t: [on his knees, bleeding] Well. Well. There it is.

[strangely calm] The chair is right there, {target}. Someone is going to sit in it. You, me, or the next one of us who walks down those stairs. Choose. I am curious, even now; I think I will be curious to the end.

q14_res_kill.t: [closing his eyes] He chose right, then. Good. Good. I am so tired of choosing.

q14_res_gauntlet.t: [laughing weakly] Chains. Amara — Amara, you have won, do you hear me — you have —
[quiet] Fine. A window. Every week. Fine.

q14_res_usurp.t: [grinning through blood] THERE. There it is. I was right about you.
[dying] It is warm, is it not. The chair. It is so warm.

q14_res_walk.t: [bewildered] You — no. No, you cannot simply — it is RIGHT THERE —
[alone, as you climb] ...it is right there.

q14_boss_challenge.t: [cold] I will challenge the strongest among you.

q14_boss_survived.t: [hard] You will not stop me, you will join our sister and the rest.

q14_boss_killed.t: [quiet] One more murder, one more sacrifice on my road to God Hood.

q14_final_open.t: [controlled] The Council has your evidence. My claim to the city is finished, and the war I prepared will not happen. You have cost me an army and years of work.
[cold] You have not stopped the succession. Morrak left part of his power in each of his children. I have taken it from those I killed. Baba taught me how to use it.

q14_final_anger.t: [hard] I killed him. He knew what I wanted, and he stood between us. He chose to die protecting you. I went there prepared to kill him.

q14_final_justice.t: [cold] The Council would keep me in chains until it could decide how to execute me. You may prefer that. I do not.

q14_final_truth.t: [measured] Then ask. You have read enough of my correspondence to deserve an answer from me.

q14_final_reports.t: [measured] My couriers brought reports from the roads, the mines and the city. I know how you reached me.

q14_final_amara_dead.t: [quiet] Amara is dead. She went there to bargain for my life, and you killed her. Tell me again how far you are willing to go for someone you love.

q14_final_amara_here.t: [hard] Amara. I asked you to hold the gate. Now you stand beside the person who means to kill me.

q14_final_amara_spared.t: [quiet] You let Amara live. I had expected you to kill anyone I put between us.

q14_final_folake_dead.t: [cold] Folake offered you information. You killed her. My guards reported what happened on her floor.

q14_final_folake_arrested.t: [measured] You had Folake arrested. She knew enough to ruin me, and you kept her alive to give evidence. That was a costly loss.

q14_final_folake_bargain.t: [dry] Folake offered you my death in return for the Consortium. One of her servants brought me the terms. She always did know what she wanted.

q14_final_grove_peace.t: [measured] You reached an agreement with the druids. They let you through their wood. I had only enemies there.

q14_final_grove_retreat.t: [measured] You drove the druids from the path. Their elders survived. My scouts saw them withdraw into the wood.

q14_final_grukhar_dead.t: [cold] Grukhar offered you the letters for his life. You killed him and took them. You had already been offered another way.

q14_final_grukhar_spared.t: [dry] Grukhar gave you the letters, and you let him leave. A useful bargain. I doubt the miners thanked you for it.

q14_final_flood.t: [hard] You opened the sluice while the prisoners were still below. Beau died with them. You knew they had not reached the stairs.

q14_final_rescue.t: [measured] You held the valve room until the prisoners were clear. That cost you time and put your company at risk. You could have opened the sluice sooner.

q14_final_segun.t: [dismissive] Segun and his men failed to hold the stairs. I paid him well to keep you out. It seems I overestimated him.

q14_final_accuse.t: [insistent] You have killed people who offered you another way. You had reasons for each of them. I have reasons too. Do you believe Morrak cares which of us can defend those reasons?

q14_final_mercy.t: [measured] You spared people I expected you to kill. Some of them helped you reach me. I misjudged what you could achieve that way.

q14_final_rebuttal.t: [cold] You are responsible for your choices. I am responsible for mine. I will not pretend otherwise.

q14_final_regret.t: [cold] Regret will not bring them back. You still have to decide what to do with me.

q14_final_mercy_reply.t: [measured] I do. I thought mercy would make you easier to stop. I was wrong.

q14_final_questions.t: [steady] You wanted answers. What else do you need to know?

q14_final_lineage.t: [measured] Baba Olusegun brought me the temple records. He found my mother’s name and traced what happened to her child. Adigun had paid him to educate me. He gave me considerably more than my father intended.
[cold] At first I had only his word and the records. Then he found another of Morrak’s children. I killed the man and felt his power pass into me. After that, I paid for the searches myself.

q14_final_rescue_truth.t: [controlled] Morrak’s priests had gathered children for a sacrifice. They believed our deaths could restore him. Tesfaye and the Wardens attacked before they could finish. He found you alive. He counted me among the dead.
[bitter] Someone came back through the chapel afterwards and found me breathing. I survived. In time, Adigun took me into his house. I knew none of this until Baba found the reports.

q14_final_blame.t: [strained] That is what his report says. I have read it many times. He believed I was dead. He was wrong. He left, and he never came back.
[hard] No, surviving gave me no right to murder him. I wanted you dead, and he would not let me have you. That was the choice I made.

q14_final_father.t: [measured] Adigun paid for the ruined ore and the bandits. He wanted the city frightened enough to pay his prices. A war would have closed his trade routes. When he learned I was buying votes to send the army into Calder, he tried to stop me.
[cold] By then, his couriers were taking my orders. They carried payments to the men hunting our kin. He did not understand what I was doing until he found the death notices.

q14_final_trap_killed.t: [measured] I sent you to his meeting and arranged the witnesses. You killed him. My men told the guards what they had seen, and I accused you. With him dead and you in custody, I could take control of the Consortium.

q14_final_trap_spared.t: [measured] You refused to kill him. I could not let him leave that room alive, so I killed him myself. Then I called the guards. My men supported my accusation, and you were standing beside his body.

q14_final_trap.t: [measured] I arranged the meeting, the witnesses and the guards. Adigun died, you went to prison, and I took control of the Consortium.

q14_final_rite.t: [measured] The war would have given me enough power to claim Morrak’s realm outright. Without it, I need another divine soul to force a passage. Once inside, I can bind the power still held there.
[cold] It will take time. That is why I intend to kill you before you can follow me.

q14_final_hiwot.t: [cold] Hiwot carries the same blood. Tesfaye raised two of Morrak’s children at Lanternhold. Baba found her name beside yours. His rite can bind her soul even after death.

q14_final_plea_reply.t: [firm] Get up, Amara. I know what you are offering. I will not spend the rest of my life in that cell.

q14_final_last.t: [hard] I have answered you. Now decide what you came here to do.

q14_final_draw.t: [hard] Then fight me. I will not ask you to forgive me.

q14_final_power.t: [cold] You understand what I have done to reach this point, and you still want to continue it. Very well. You will have to kill me first.

q14_final_abducted.t: [cold] While you followed me down here, my remaining guards went to the inn. They brought Hiwot through the servants’ passage. She is behind the altar.

q14_final_absent.t: [cold] My remaining guards found Hiwot before you reached the temple. They brought her through the servants’ passage. She is behind the altar.

q14_final_dead_sister.t: [cold] Hiwot’s soul has already returned to our father’s realm. Baba bound it to this altar. I did not need to find her alive.

q14_final_ritual.t: [breathless] You broke my army. You have beaten me here. But you brought the rite within reach.

q14_final_crossing.t: [strained] The passage is open. By the time you reach me, I will have bound the throne.

q14_final_realm.t: [furious] You followed me. Before the binding was complete.
[hard] Then I will finish this myself. Your soul will join hers.

q1_catchup.t: [breathless] {target}! Oh, thank every saint that listens. I saw you both leave and I followed — yes, I know, I was not supposed to — and then I saw the torches, and the big one in the black armour, and I ran the other way, because I am not brave. I am only fast.
[quieter] He is dead. Tesfaye. I saw him fall. I can't believe we left him there. He should be with us.
[urgent] Tell me what the big one said to him. I was too far; I saw his mouth move and Tesfaye shake his head. What did he want?

q1_wren_kind.t: [steadying] He wanted you. By name. Then it was never about Tesfaye at all. — Close. Yes. I can do close. I have his letter; it was in his coat. An inn on the Shore Road, and two names, Beau and Delphine. He must have meant for us to go to them.

q1_wren_cold.t: [stung, then flat] Right. I am fine. — I have his letter. An inn and two names. You may read it when you have finished being a wall.

q1_wren_dark.t: [uneasy] "What you are." He said that? — You sounded like him just then. Not Tesfaye. The other one. [softer] There is a letter. An inn, two names. Let us go and be alive first. You can be terrible later.

q1_join.t: [firm] I am coming with you. I can pick locks and keep watch while you sleep. Besides, if you leave me here, I will only have to follow you again.

q2_road.t: [reading] "The Open Hand, on the Shore Road, past the salt-flats. Ask for Beau and Delphine. They are Wardens, and they were my friends before you were born. Trust them as you would trust me." — That is all it says. He never wasted ink.
[thinking] Wardens. He never once said that word in twenty years, and now it is the first thing he wants us to know. That is the first thing I am asking them.

q2_pair_hiwot.t: [low, to you] Do not tell them anything. We do not know them.

q2_wolves.t: [low] Wolves. Road wolves, the big grey kind — Tesfaye said they only come down to the road when the hills are hungry.
[very quiet] Something has made the hills hungry.

q2_cassian_hiwot.t: [sceptical] Alone. Who sends one squire to a wolf den? What did you do to your Order?

q2_morwin_hiwot.t: [quickly] Neither. We are pilgrims. Going to the shrine at — the shrine.

q2_notice.t: [picking up the paper] He was carrying this. Your face, and a bounty, and a seal of an iron hand in red wax. No name.

[quiet] Somebody with a great deal of money wants you dead badly enough to send two men in one night and a third to wait at the one door Tesfaye trusted. I am keeping this. Somebody at that inn will know the mark.

q3_south_hiwot.t: [thinking] A locked drawer in his study. I never got it open, and I tried twice, which he knew, because he moved the key. He never moved anything else.
[quiet] It is still there. Whatever it is.

q4_down.t: [low] It smells like wet dog and hot metal. Four levels of that, going down.
[quiet] Keep your light up. I can't see where these stairs end.

q4_letters.t: [reading] "Keep the ore fouled until the spring shipment. Gorruk holds the north road." And a name — Femi, at the inn in Thornbury.
[quiet] Tesfaye died over a shipping schedule. That cannot be the whole of it. It cannot.

q4_camp_hiwot.t: [quiet, at the fire] Delphine. Was he a good Warden? Tesfaye. He never talked about it, and I have been wondering all day whether that was because it was bad, or because it was good.

q5_verlan_pocket.t: [murmuring] Map, seal, and a very old sausage. He did not feel a thing.
[low] Past Holloway Vale, under the oaks. There is a note about the road being watched.

q5_camp.t: [whispering] Or I go over the palisade and open the back gate while every eye is on the front.

q5_camp_quiet.t: [breathless] The back gate is open. Two sentries were sleeping, and one of them is going to wake with a headache and no boots.
[low] The big tent is the lord's. There is a man chained in it who looks as though he still has jokes left.

q5_camp_storm.t: [resigned] Loud, then. Go for the one with the horns first; the rest will look to him.

q6_forest.t: [low] Old trees. Very old, very big. Things in the branches that stop moving when we look.
[a breath] I will go first. No. I will not. You go first.

q6_wyverns.t: [appalled] It has a sting on its tail. Its tail has a sting.

q7_cages.t: [sick] They keep them in cages between shifts. Like dogs. Worse than dogs; I have seen dogs kept better than this.

q7_valve.t: [frantic] Beau is below with the chain-gang. If you turn that wheel he drowns with them.

q7_flood_now.t: [hollow] He was coming up. We could hear the chains.

q7_papers.t: [reading] Three names at the Consortium's tower in the city. Adigun Adeyinka, Bankole, Rotimi.
[quiet] The road north is open now. There is nothing between us and the Gate but the Gate.

q7_mine_umbra_none.t: [low] The druids wanted this mine shut down too.
[dry] We could have had their help. Instead, we picked a fight with them. That was clever of us.

q8_sewers.t: [gagging] I have been in a mine, a fortress and a spider nest this month, and THIS is the worst. This is the worst place.

q8_door.t: [whispering] Doorman. I can get us past him. He will not even remember we were here.

q8_door_wren.t: [smug] Side window. He is asleep on his feet. I told you.

q8_door_force.t: [sighing] Loud again. I am keeping a list.

q8_faces.t: [horrified] That is the merchant's face. That is his FACE and it is not him. Nothing is behind the eyes.

q9_lobby.t: [whispering] A clerk. Two guards. A very long list of names on his desk, and we are not on it.

q9_lobby_talk.t: [impressed] He BELIEVED you. Olamide's name still opens doors. Third floor, he says. Do not touch anything.

q9_lobby_fight.t: [flat] So much for quiet. Stairs. Go.

q9_lobby_wren.t: [hushed] Got it. There is a name at the bottom in red: "the ward — as agreed." Whatever we do up there, somebody upstairs already knows we are coming.

q9_top.t: [stunned] Lanternhold. They went HOME. The three men who paid to kill Tesfaye are sitting in his library. — The drawer. Delphine, the locked drawer. We are going to be in that room.

q10_ring_hiwot.t: [suspicious] How did you know Tesfaye? I lived in that keep twenty years and I never once saw you.

q10_home.t: [strange] It smells the same. Ink and dust and the brothers' lentils. I thought it would feel like home, and it feels like a trap.

q10_catacombs_hiwot.t: [brightly] None of us. We are pilgrims.

q10_double.t: [Hiwot's voice, wrong] {target}. Thank the saints. I got separated — come here, come HERE, we have to go —

q10_double_question.t: [the real Hiwot, furious] The HONEY. It was the honey, and Brother Yonas still blames the cat — that thing wearing my face does not know that, so STAB IT.

q10_shore.t: [shaking] Out. We are out. I am never going home again, am I.
[small] Sanni sent us into that room. Then he told the guards we'd murdered his father. He had this planned before we ever left the city.

q11_posters.t: [reading] "Wanted, for the murder of Grand Duke Ayodele and of the Consortium summit at Lanternhold: the ward of Tesfaye, and company." That is your face. That is a BAD drawing of your face.
[quiet] The street is full of it: Emeka Obi is dead. A man called Segun Marr commands the Gauntlet now, and he is the one who signed this.

q11_doors.t: [thinking] Three doors. Adebayo, if we can save him. Folake, if you can stand her. Or Tunde Softfoot and a debt.

q11_alleg_gauntlet.t: [nodding] The Duke. All right. I like a Duke who owes us.

q11_alleg_consortium.t: [uneasy] Folake. I do not trust her smile. I do not trust anything about her. But she does have a door.

q11_alleg_thieves.t: [grinning] Tunde! Yes. I was hoping you would say that. Thieves are honest about what they are.

q12_steps.t: [itching] I hate silk. I hate silk SO much. — There he is. On the dais. Smiling. He has a lovely smile. I want to put it through a wall.

q12_dukes_korvath.t: [shouting] The dukes — {target}, the DUKES — we cannot hold them if you run at him —

q13_return.t: [stiff, bandaged] I heard you were going under the city without me. Absolutely not.
[fierce] I am stitched, I am furious, and I still open locks better than anyone here. Move over.

q13_maze.t: [hushed] The thieves' maze. I can read it — half of it is Lanternhold locks, the cheap kind. Follow me exactly.

q13_maze_follow.t: [murmuring] Left. Again. Not that one. — Through. Nobody bled. Tell Tesfaye I was paying attention.

q13_maze_cut.t: [groaning] Straight through. Fine. The loud list is getting long.

q14_sanctum.t: [whispering] It is warm down here. It should not be warm.
[fierce] Whatever he says in there — you are Tesfaye's. Not his. Tesfaye's.

q14_mirrors.t: [horrified] That is ME. That is all of us. They are wearing US.

banter.t: [shouting] The left one! The left one is looking at YOU!
[breathless] Still with you. Keep going!
[gleeful] Got his purse. And his knife. And his — never mind, keep fighting.

q14_final_warning.t: [urgent] The marks on the floor! They lead to the altar. Get away from them!

q14_final_soul.t: [weak] I can hear you. He has bound me to the throne. Break his hold before he can finish.

q14_final_choice.t: [quiet] He’s gone. I can feel the power he took, and yours. It is holding this place open.
[steady] If you let it all go, I can come back with you. You will lose Morrak’s blood, and any claim to his throne. If you keep it, you can take his place. I cannot come back that way.

q14_final_restored.t: [unsteady] I can breathe. I thought I would never...
[soft] You came back for me. Let’s get out of here. Please.

q14_final_farewell.t: [quiet] I wanted to go home with you. I hope you remember that.

q2_pair.t: [bright] Well now — look at this, Winston. Two little travellers on a big empty road, and one of them holding a sword like it might bite.
[delighted] Desmond. This is Winston. We are going the same way as you, which is a coincidence, and we are very good in a fight, which is not.

q2_where_lie.t: [gleeful] Lying. Look at the hands, Winston — the hands always know. I like them already.
[sing-song] No worry yourself. Everybody lies to us. We are used to it.

q2_pair_yes.t: [sing-song] You hear that, Winston? We have friends now. — No worry yourself, {target}. I bite only the ones you tell me to.

q7_papers.t: [soft] Those papers. Names, seals, routes. The people we answer to would pay plenty to read them before the Gauntlet does.
[softer] Let Winston copy them tonight, and we stay quiet and useful for as long as you like.

q7_papers_refuse.t: [very calm] Then we go, and you will see us again, and it won't be as friends.
[light] It never was, really. I did tell you stories like yours get told badly.

q9_betrayal.t: [bright] {target}! You found us! We work here now, you see it? It pays better than you did.
[giggling] Winston says we should kill you quick. Me, I would like to take my time.

banter.t: [giggling] Oh, he is BURNING. Look at him go, man.
[sing-song] More, more, more —
[delighted] Come on, then. I'm right here.

q2_pair.t: [flat] He talks. I do the rest.

q2_pair_ask.t: [level] Before anybody says yes or no: where are two children walking so fast, with one blade between them and no pack? People with a reason walk like that. I want the reason.

q2_where_truth.t: [thoughtful] The Open Hand. That's a Warden house; everybody on this coast knows it. So you are walking toward trouble, not away from it, and you are honest about it. Both of those are useful to me.

q2_where_refuse.t: [unbothered] Fair. It is. Then here is mine, so we are even.

q2_pair_offer.t: [flat] We are hired blades between hirings, and the road is bad for two and better for four. Say yes or say no, but say it before the light goes. I do not like this stretch after dark.

q2_pair_who.t: [dry] You want the true answer or the polite one? Polite: two men with skills and no master this month. True: we work for people who pay to know things, and right now they would like to know why iron costs three times what it did last year. You are not the thing we are looking for. You are on the road to it.

q2_pair_vess.t: [a sigh] Desmond is well the way a fire is well. He can raise the dead for a little while and he laughs when the dead fall down again. I keep him pointed the right way. I have done it since we were boys and I am tired, but I am still doing it.

q2_pair_no.t: [unbothered] Then go easy. If you change your mind, we will be the ones ahead of you with the fire lit. — Desmond. Walk.

q3_lessa_winston.t: [flat] Before the knives, girl. What's the rate? Two hundred, still, or has it gone up since Merle?

q3_lessa_winston_after.t: [dry] Thinking about who can afford to keep raising it. Carry on.

q3_tollan_winston.t: [flat] Mayor. Who takes your wagons north? One buyer, or many?

q3_tollan_winston_after.t: [low, to himself] One buyer. That's what they wanted to know. — Go on, man.

q4_healing.t: [firm] That chief keeps healing. I've shut it off for now. Hit him before it wears off.

q4_grukhar_winston.t: [flat] Which spring shipment, priest? Whose wagons?

q5_camp.t: [calm] Three ways into a camp like that, man. Loud, quiet, or invited.
[dry] Desmond and I can be invited. Recruiters never look too close at faces that frighten them.

q5_camp_recruits.t: [murmuring] Walk like you already killed somebody today. Desmond — no smiling.
[low] We are in. The big tent is Gorruk's. There is a chained man inside; don't look at him yet.

q5_camp_storm.t: [flat] Loud. Sawa — fine. The one with the horns is a sergeant; the rest look to him. Kill him first and they look to nobody.

q7_study_winston.t: [flat] Two sets of books, mage. Which one goes to the Gate?

q7_papers.t: [flat] He means it. So do I. It is the only thing we were ever on this road for, and I told you I would say so before the day came. This is the day.

q7_papers_who.t: [level] The Umbral Hand. You have heard the name; everybody has, and everybody pretends they haven't. Merchants, mostly, of a kind. They want to know who is cornering iron on this coast, and why, and they don't much care who dies of the knowing.

q7_papers_give.t: [nodding] Copies. Fair. You won't regret keeping us.
[dry] You may regret Desmond. That is a separate matter.

q8_door.t: [flat] Doorman. Leave him to me. Everybody has a price, and his is written on his face.

q8_door_fennick.t: [flat] Thirty gold and the man has gone for a very long lunch.

q8_door_force.t: [dry] Through him, then. Mind — a man that size falls slow.

q9_betrayal.t: [flat] Nothing personal, man. You said that yourself once.

banter.t: [flat] Back lane. Poison. Done.
[calm] Stay close. Don't give them a gap.
[dry] Desmond, stop laughing, it puts them off.

q2_cassian.t: [formal, out of breath] Hold — with respect, hold! Do not go into the den, señor — señora — forgive me, I do not know which, and I have run a long way.
[straightening] Santiago, squire of the Order of the Dawning Flame. I have been sent to clear these wolves from the road, and I have been sent alone.

q2_cassian_answer.t: [reddening, honest] Nothing. That is the difficulty. A knight who has done nothing is sent to do something, and a wolf den on a road nobody uses is the something. I will confess to you, as I would to no one in the Order, that I am not certain I can.

q2_cassian_alone.t: [honest] I will confess to you, as I would to no one in the Order, that I am not certain I can. I have never fought anything that was not a straw man.

q2_cassian_order.t: [earnest] An order of knights sworn to the sun and the sunrise: to be first into the dark and last out of it. Our chapter house is far south of here, in the sun-lands, where I was born. The Order sent me north to learn what the roads are like. I am learning.

q2_cassian_tease.t: [reddening, then honest] Prayers, mostly. And the sword, and how to stand still while people say unkind things — which, with respect, you are doing very well.

q2_cassian_join.t: [relieved] God keep you for it. Then I will take the front, because that is what I am for, and you will tell me if I am doing it wrong.

q2_cassian_no.t: [formal, hurt] Of course. God go with you, then. I will — I will manage.

q5_patrol.t: [uneasy] Burning Gauntlet. A patrol, this far south of the city. They have someone at sword-point — and with respect, by her look, she is not from anywhere near here.

q5_patrol_cassian.t: [formal, tight] A priestess of what, señora? Say it. I would know what I am deciding about.

q5_patrol_cassian_after.t: [quietly] It might. — {target}. Your word decides it. Not mine.

q5_cassian_leaves.t: [quietly] I cannot ride beside a company that shelters what this one shelters. I have prayed on it, and I have tried to find a way, and I cannot.
[formal] If your company changes, you will find me at the Open Hand. I hope it does. I hope that very much. God keep you, {target}.

q9_floor_cassian.t: [low] With respect. You do not have to answer her. She is bargaining.

bond_first.t: [hesitant] The training yard was easy. You knew the other man would stop.
[honest] In a real fight, I still want to run. I worry that one day I will.

bond_first_reply.t: [relieved] Thank you. I needed to hear that from someone who had actually seen me fight.

bond_second.t: [easier] I wrote home. Mostly about the people I have met. My mother would worry if I described the fighting.
[fond] She runs a bakery. I used to get up before dawn to carry flour. I complained every morning. Now I miss it.

bond_second_reply.t: [warm] There is a stool by the oven where I used to sleep between deliveries. Mother still keeps it there. She says my room is too far from the work.

bond_interest.t: [shy] I would like that too. May we take a little time? I want to know you better.

bond_later.t: [gentle] Of course. Tell me when you are ready. We can still enjoy each other's company.

q9_romance.t: [nervous] I enjoy the time we spend together. More than I know how to say properly.
[earnest] When we have a quiet evening, may I take you to supper? Just the two of us.

q9_romance_yes.t: [pleased] Supper, then. I know a decent place. I will try to get through the evening without saluting you.

q9_romance_no.t: [bravely] Then I am glad I said it, and I will not say it again. Thank you for hearing it.

banter.t: [shouting] For the Dawning Flame! — forgive me. Habit.
[earnest] On me! I can take it!
[strained] I am fine! I am — mostly fine!

q2_morwin.t: [drawling, on the inn steps] Well, look here. Two of you, and a paper in my pocket with one face on it. Now which one's the ward of Tesfaye of Lanternhold? Don't all shout at once.

q2_morwin_hiwot_reply.t: [amused] Pilgrims. With that face, that the paper's got drawn near perfect. Nice try, little sister.
[unhurried] Merle. I'm the fella they send when the first fella don't come back. Now I'll say this once: I'd sooner do this out here than in Delphine's yard. That woman scares me.

q2_morwin_alone.t: [unhurried] Merle. I'm the fella they send when the first fella don't come back. I'd sooner do this out here than in Delphine's yard. That woman scares me.

q2_morwin_name.t: [chuckling] Same as always. A seal, no name. Iron hand on red wax, pressed hard, like whoever did it was angry at the wax. If you want a name you'll have to go up the road a good deal further than me.

q2_morwin_how.t: [a shrug] The old man had two friends in the whole world, and they run this inn. Anybody who knew him knew that. Whoever's paying knew him.

q2_morwin_kill.t: [grinning] Now there's the temper the paper warned me about.

q2_morwin_inn.t: [cursing] Oh, that's low. That's — I hear the door. All right. All right, quick then.

q2_selene.t: [stammering, warm] You're — y-you're his. Tesfaye's. I'd know that coat anywhere; he w-wore it the day we met. Come in. Come in out of the road.
[quiet] Del. It's the ward. He sent the ward.

q2_beau_seal.t: [low] Del. The p-paper the man on the steps had. Look at the seal. Iron hand, red wax.
[steadier] That's the mark on the ore wagons. The ones that come up from Dunmere and go north. I've seen it a hundred times at the ford.

q7_gate.t: [grim] Slaves. They're w-working slaves in there. I can hear the chains from here.
[steady] I'm going to the bottom for 'em, {target}. Whatever else we do today. Tell me you're with me.

q7_dorran_with.t: [fierce] Good. G-good. The front's mine. Nothing gets past me today.

q7_dorran_mission.t: [quiet] There'll be time. I'll m-make time.

q7_cage_beau.t: [urgent] The ch-chain-gang. Where do they keep them between shifts?

q7_flood_wait.t: [shouting from below] Coming up! Nineteen of 'em and me! Hold the d-door — they're right behind us!

q7_after.t: [exhausted] Nineteen. Every one. Not one left in the dark.
[quiet] Thank you for holding. I heard you say it. I won't forget it.

banter.t: [steady] H-hold the line. Hold it. Nothing gets past.
[grunting] Shield's up. Hit 'em while they hit me.
[shouting] Del! Behind you!

q2_selene.t: [warm, gentle] I'm Delphine, Beau's wife. Your late stepfather, Tesfaye, was an old friend of ours. Sit down, honey. Beau, get the good bread.

[steady] He wrote to us from Lanternhold every year for twenty years. Said you and Hiwot were growing up in that keepers' library, getting into everything he tried to keep you out of. His last letter said if you came here without him, we were to keep you safe.
[quiet, direct] So. How did he die? All of it. Don't you spare me.

q2_how_armour.t: [very still] Black plate. Asked for you by name.

[to Beau] Beau. The letter from the spring. He said if a big man in black iron ever came asking, we weren't to fight him, we were to run with the child and ask questions after. I thought he'd gone strange.

q2_how_quick.t: [gently] That's a kindness, and a lie, and I'll take both. Thank you, sugar.
[to Beau] Beau. Whoever did it knew where Tesfaye was, and Tesfaye chose that library because nobody knew. Somebody talked.

q2_how_refuse.t: [soft] Then don't. But you'll tell Beau when you can; he loved him too, and he's worse at waiting than I am.

q2_selene_seal.t: [looking] It is. The Iron Consortium's mark — the trading house out of the Gate that's been buying every bar on this coast since the ore went bad.

[slowly] So the folks paying to kill Tesfaye's ward are the folks who own the iron. That ain't two stories, honey. That's one. Now you ask me whatever you need to, and then we decide what he'd have done.

q2_selene_wardens.t: [matter-of-fact] Folks who keep the balance between the towns and the wild, and between the strong and the weak, when the law's too far off to do it. Tesfaye was one, before the library. So are we. It don't pay, and nobody thanks you, and you do it anyway. That's the whole of the oath.

q2_selene_why.t: [carefully] I don't know, and I won't pretend I do. I know Tesfaye hid you like a man hides a lit candle in a wind, and never said from what. A trading house don't spend two hundred on spite. They think you're worth it, or they think you're dangerous, and I can't tell you which from here.

q2_selene_trust.t: [softening] He'd have followed the money. The iron's gone bad since spring — tools snapping, blades cracking, every smith from here to the Gate cussing — and the ore comes up out of Dunmere. The Consortium's mark is on the wagons and on your bounty. So we go to Dunmere and find out what's wrong with that ore, and I'd bet my house we find out who wants you dead the same day.

q2_selene_alone.t: [flat] You'll go with us or you'll go over my husband, and he's a big man. Tesfaye asked. I don't break a promise to a dead friend because a child is grieving and rude about it.

q2_join.t: [decisive] Beau, get the shields. We're going to Dunmere.
[to you] I'll tell you what: you're Tesfaye's, and Tesfaye's is ours. That's all the reason we need, and it's all the reason you're getting tonight.

q3_south.t: [calm] Dunmere's two days south. Mining town, hard folk, honest as far as it goes. The mayor's a man called Gethin Pryce; he'll be sweating, and he'll pay.
[dry] Stay off the river road after dark. Gnolls come down it. I know because I've buried the people who didn't listen.

q3_south_hiwot.t: [casual, not casual] Hiwot. You grew up in that library with him. Did he keep letters? Anything from the Gate, anything with that iron seal on it?

q3_south_hiwot_reply.t: [nodding] Then it's still there. Remember that, both of you. If this road ever bends back toward Lanternhold, that drawer's the first door we open.

q3_ithrel_selene.t: [sharp] A year hunting one ogre alone, and the Wardens never heard of you. Why didn't you come to us?

q3_ithrel_selene_after.t: [a beat] ...It ain't. Damn it. It should be.

q3_tollan_selene.t: [level] Gethin. Before the crews. Who's been buying your bad ore since spring, and who's been selling the smiths good iron since?

q3_tollan_selene_after.t: [to Beau, quiet] Same hand. Beau, I told you. Buy the ore cheap because it's bad, sell the iron dear because it's the only good iron left. Somebody's making that ore bad on purpose.

q4_down.t: [calm] Mind the timbers; half of them are rotten. If the kobolds are as thick as the mayor says, we go slow and we keep the healer in the middle. That's me, honey. Don't argue.

q4_flooded.t: [calm] Water on the second level, and not from any spring. Somebody opened a channel and let the river in on purpose.
[thoughtful] Kobolds don't plan. Kobolds dig where they're pointed. Whoever's pointing them is below us, and has been for weeks.

q4_grukhar_selene.t: [flat] Your orders. Sealed how? Iron hand, red wax, pressed hard.

q4_grukhar_selene_after.t: [to you, low] On a wagon, on a bounty, and now on an altar. That's three. — Go on, honey. He's yours to deal with.

q4_letters.t: [reading] "To the priest, from Femi at the Thornbury inn. Keep the ore fouled until the spring shipment. Gorruk holds the north road; do not use it without his mark."
[calm] A courier, and a bandit lord above him, and above them somebody who buys with a seal instead of a name. The mine was only the bottom of this.

q4_camp_selene.t: [after a moment] He was the best of us, sugar. And he quit. Those ain't two different stories either.

q5_inn_selene.t: [pleasant, deadly] Hollister says you've had that room since the spring, Femi. Now I'll tell you what puzzles me. What does a wine merchant sell for six months in a town with one inn, that already has a cellar?

q5_inn_selene_after.t: [to you] He's got papers, honey. I'd like to see them.

q5_letters_selene.t: [level] A name, Cal. Not a seal. Somebody at the Consortium signs for this. Who?

q6_forest.t: [calm] The Mirkhollow. Old wood — older than the Wardens, older than the Gate. It's got its own druids, and they ain't friends of ours; we keep the balance by law and they keep it by blood.
[quiet] Keep to the deer paths. Anything down here that looks like a road was made by something with a great many legs.

q6_grove_selene.t: [steady] None of us. The iron's what we took off the men who are poisoning your river. We're here to shut their mine.

q6_gate.t: [calm] Iron livery on the guards. Consortium men. And the tall one — Kestrel. A sword for hire who'll guard anything for anybody. I've crossed him before.
