[flat] He won't talk. Don't waste your breath on it.

q6_fire.t: [quiet] Sit a minute. The forest's loud tonight and I want to say a thing before I lose the nerve.
[soft] Tesfaye wrote to us every year about you. Twenty letters. I feel like I've known you since you could walk, and I met you a month ago. It's a strange thing. It ain't an unwelcome one.

q6_fire_letters.t: [fond] The first year, that you'd learned to walk and walked straight into the library. The seventh, that you'd stolen honey from the brothers and let a cat take the blame. The last — that you were ready, and that he wasn't.

q6_fire_warm.t: [a soft laugh] Enough. Yeah. That's a very Tesfaye amount.
[warm] Goodnight, {target}. Wake me if the trees start walking.

q6_fire_deflect.t: [quiet] All right. Get some rest. We can talk another time.

q6_fire_dorran.t: [fond] He is. He also snores like a bear in a barrel, so the fortune runs both ways.
[warm] Goodnight, {target}. Don't you tell him I said that.

q7_valve.t: [tight] Beau's still down there. {target}. Beau is still down there.

q7_flood_now.t: [broken] He was coming up. He was coming up. You heard the chains. You heard him.

q7_after_dead.t: [hollow] Olamide's papers. Names in the city. Take them. I don't care.
[cold] I'll finish this road because Tesfaye asked it of me. Don't you speak to me until it's done.

q7_papers.t: [reading] Olamide wrote to three men at the Consortium's tower in Varenholm's Gate. Adigun Adeyinka. Bankole. Rotimi.
[calm] Adeyinka. Cal heard right. The bandits are broke and the mine's drowned, and the road north is open, and so, at last, are the names.

q8_faces.t: [disturbed] That's the merchant's face and it ain't the merchant. Look at the eyes, honey. Nothing lives behind 'em.
[hard] Shape-thieves. They wear you after they kill you. Don't let one get behind you.

q9_lobby.t: [murmuring] A clerk with a list and two guards who are paid to believe him.

q9_lobby_talk.t: [quiet] He believed it. Third floor. Don't touch anything.

q9_top.t: [reading] Adigun Adeyinka, Bankole, Rotimi. Gone to Lanternhold — to LANTERNHOLD — for a summit with the keepers.
[cold] The three men behind all of this are sitting in the library you grew up in.

q9_family.t: [warm] You're family, honey. You don't have to face this alone. Get some rest. We leave for Lanternhold in the morning.

q10_summit_selene.t: [flat] Then answer me this, Adeyinka, before anybody decides anything. The iron hand in red wax on the ore wagons. Whose seal is that?

q10_summit_selene_after.t: [to you, quiet] Your seal on the wagons and his on the bounty. Same wax. I've been right since the inn, honey, and I ain't glad of it.

q10_double_strike.t: [sharp] Two of 'em — and the real Hiwot was BEHIND it, {target}, you cut her — she's breathing. She's breathing. She ain't walking out of here on her own.
[grim] I'll get her to the surface. Go on without us.

q10_double_listen.t: [urgent] That ain't who it looks like. {target}. That is NOT them. It's already reaching for your throat — move!

q10_double_strike_alone.t: [grim] That wasn't him, and you knew it before I did. It's dead. There's two more behind it wearing faces I don't know — keep moving.

q10_shore.t: [hard] Sanni sent us after his father. Then he called the guards on us. With Adigun dead and us wanted for murder, who is left to stop him?

q11_posters.t: [cold] Grand Duke Ayodele was murdered last night and they've put your name on it. Obi's dead too. A man called Segun Marr runs the Gauntlet now.
[calm] Kolade will be sworn in as the new Duke within days. He's moved everything into place while we were underground.

q11_doors.t: [calm] Three ways into that palace, and we won't get a second try.
[measured] Adebayo's dying; cure him and the Gauntlet is ours. Folake offered a way in, for a price. And the thieves under the Undervault will sell us a door if we owe 'em after.

q11_alleg_gauntlet.t: [approving] Lawfully. Tesfaye would've said the same, and then he'd have cheated a little. Let's go find the Duke.

q11_alleg_consortium.t: [flat] Her. Fine. I'll hold my nose. Don't you let her hold anything of yours.

q11_alleg_thieves.t: [dry] Tunde Softfoot never forgets a debt. Neither will you. All right — the Undervault.

q12_steps.t: [low] Borrowed silks, real steel, two invitations. Everybody in that hall is either a guest or a shape-thief, and there's no way to tell which till the knives come out.
[calm] Stay near the dukes. He needs them dead more than he needs you.

q12_dukes_korvath.t: [shouting] The dukes are DYING, {target} — we can't hold both if you run at him —

q13_steps_selene.t: [flat] Where's Emeka Obi, Marr? He had a wife on Tanner Street. She'd like to know where to put the flowers.

q14_sanctum.t: [low] A temple to a dead god, still swept, still lit. Somebody's been praying here for twenty years.
[steady] Whatever he says at that altar, {target}, you remember who raised you. Then you do what you have to.

q14_mirrors.t: [cold] Our faces. Every one. Kill 'em quick; don't look at the eyes.

banter.t: [calm] Breathe, honey. The one in front's slower than he looks.
[sharp] Mind the mage. I'll mind the rest.
[dry] If you die, I will be very put out. Don't.

q3_ithrel.t: [quiet, from the treeline] Forgive me. I do not mean to alarm you. I have walked beside your road for an hour, deciding whether to speak.

[level] You are going north to the Gate, by the river road? — Then I will be plain. I am Itsuki. A year ago an ogre called Gorruk, who leads the bandit companies in the north, burned a wagon on this road. My wife was in it. I have hunted him since, alone, and alone I cannot reach him.

q3_ithrel_selene_reply.t: [calm] I did. A man at a Warden house on the coast told me the north road is not the Wardens' road. He was polite about it.

q3_ithrel_ask.t: [level] You are going towards him. I would go with you. I ask nothing else.

q3_ithrel_seal.t: [thinking] I have seen letters carried to his camp. Sealed. I did not read them; I was too far, and I am no thief. The seal was red, and pressed hard. That is all I can say honestly.

q3_ithrel_wife.t: [a long pause] Hana. Thank you for asking. No one asks. They ask about him.

q3_ithrel_yes.t: [a small bow] Then I am in your debt before I have earned my place. I will keep the rear. You will not hear me unless you need to.

q3_ithrel_no.t: [calm] I understand. I will walk on ahead of you, then. If our roads cross again, I will not ask twice.

q5_tent_ithrel.t: [very quiet] Gorruk. Where does he sleep?

q5_shot.t: [very quietly] {target}. I have him. A clean line, no cover. Say yes.

q5_shot_yes.t: [exhaling] Thank you. Whatever comes after this — thank you.

q5_shot_no.t: [tight] Alive. I have waited a year. I can wait until the end of a fight.

q5_gone.t: [cold] He walked out of that tent because you wished it. I will find him myself.

q5_dead.t: [quietly] It is done. I thought I would feel taller. I feel as though I could sleep for a year.
[soft] I will stay, if you will have me. There is nothing else I was for.

bond_first.t: [low] I have spent so long following tracks that I have given little thought to what comes after.
[tired] I cannot go back to the life I had with my wife. I do not yet know what else I want.

bond_first_reply.t: [quiet] I would like to stay. It helps to have people expecting me back.

bond_second.t: [thoughtful] I used to guide travellers through the woods. Some had never slept outside. They would wake me over every rustle.
[faintly amused] One paid me extra to keep the owls away. I gave him something to plug his ears.

bond_second_reply.t: [warm] I would enjoy that. There are places worth visiting without a bounty to collect.

bond_interest.t: [careful] I care for you. I need time before I can promise more. If you are willing to wait, I would like to try.

bond_later.t: [calm] Take the time you need. You know where to find me.

q9_romance.t: [low] I still miss my wife. I always will.
[quiet] But I have come to care for you too. If you feel the same, I would like us to be together.

q9_romance_yes.t: [quiet] Then we will take our time. I am glad you told me.

q9_romance_no.t: [calm] I understand. It was enough to say it. Sleep.

q11_docks_ithrel.t: [very quiet] The north road. A year ago. Were you there when the wagons burned?

q13_gorruk.t: [very quietly] Mine. You said. Say it again.

banter.t: [quiet] Loosing.
[flat] The archer is mine. Leave him.
[cold] Again.

q3_lessa.t: [smiling, from a corner table] There you are, sugar. I've been nursing this cider an hour, waiting on you. Lurleen. You don't know me, but I know that face; I've got it on paper in my pocket.
[light] Three sent before me, I hear. And one of them Merle, who I liked. So this ain't only money now. Just so you know.

q3_lessa_winston_reply.t: [amused] Three now. It goes up every time one of us don't come back. You thinking of switching sides, halfling?

q3_lessa_ask.t: [light] Well? You going to say something clever, or are we going to get on with it?

q3_lessa_why.t: [a shrug] Because I'm good at it, and because nobody else in this country pays a woman to be good at anything. You'd know, if you'd grown up anywhere but a library.

q3_lessa_fight.t: [pleased] There she is. — There he is. Whichever. Come on, then.

q3_bramm.t: [booming] — and I say AGAIN, red man, you touch that cage and I will fold you into it!

[turning] VALLAHI. Strangers. Good. Strangers, listen: Bahadır, ranger of Kalden, and this is Fındık, who is small but very brave. There is a woman in that fortress, in a cage. Yasemin. A witch of my country, and a good one.

q3_bramm_argue.t: [hot] Tell them why Vashk burns women, wizard! Tell them what your Crimson masters do with a witch's bones!

q3_bramm_rescue.t: [overjoyed] With you! Yes! Fındık, did you hear? We have friends, and they are good ones. Come — the gate is that way, and I am going through it.

q3_road_block.t: [wounded, roaring] You TOOK his coin. You looked at me and you took his coin! Then you go through me, and Fındık, and every tree in this valley — come on! COME ON!

q3_joined.t: [emphatic] We are yours, {target}. Vallahi. Where you go, we go, and anyone who says otherwise answers to Fındık.

banter.t: [roaring] FINDIK SAYS GO FOR THE EYES!
[booming] Nobody touches the witch! NOBODY! Vallahi!
[gleeful] Ha HA! Did you SEE that, canım?

q3_bramm.t: [disdainful] Kindly disregard the large gentleman; his enthusiasms are exhausting. Devendra, Crimson Wizard of Vashk. The woman in the cage is a Kalden witch, and it is quite evident that a Kalden witch loose in these hills is a calamity waiting for a date.

q3_bramm_argue.t: [coolly] Vashk and Kalden have been at war, in one form or another, since before these strangers' grandparents were born. I do not expect the large gentleman to understand policy. I expect him to understand a hundred in gold — which I am offering to you, not to him. A hundred to see her burned, and my considerable talents beside you until the Gate.

q3_bramm_why.t: [coolly] Because one witch becomes a coven, and a coven becomes a border dispute, and a border dispute becomes my problem. That I am polite about it is a courtesy, not a change of policy.

q3_bramm_coin.t: [satisfied] A sensible arrangement. The large gentleman will object; I recommend we not be near him when he does.

q3_bramm_both.t: [thin] Hold my tongue. Very well. I shall hold it most eloquently. Do not expect me to be happy about it.

banter.t: [bored] Do kindly keep them off me; I am the expensive one.
[smug] Burning. Obviously.
[sneering] Barely worth the spell.

q3_freed.t: [cold, from the cage] Thank you. I would kneel, but the bars have made it difficult.

[looking at you] You. Come closer. Something in your blood woke when you came through the fortress gate; I felt it through the bars like heat from a stove in the next room. I have read auras all my life and I have never felt one like it.
[direct] So tell me, before I decide what to do about it. When it woke — what did it want?

q3_ysolde_blood.t: [a slow nod] Honest. Good. Then I know what kind of thing it is, if not its name: something that was worshipped once, and fed. I would sooner walk beside it than behind it. Bahadır goes where I go, and Fındık goes where Bahadır goes, and so you have three. Two and a half.

q3_ysolde_nothing.t: [dry] You felt nothing. Canım, I watched your hand. — Very well; you are not ready to say it, and that is your right. I will walk beside you anyway, and I will keep watching the hand. Bahadır goes where I go.

q3_ysolde_what.t: [precise] Something that was worshipped once, and should not have been. That is as plain as I can be without lying to you. I read auras, not histories. Now answer mine.

q3_ysolde_quiet.t: [dry] As you like. I am a witch. Keeping things to myself is most of the work. I will walk beside you, and I will not say it again in front of the others. Bahadır goes where I go.

banter.t: [calm] Frost. Hold him still.
[formal] Your aura flares when you fight. Interesting.
[cool] Keep them in front of us.

q3_tollan.t: [harried, Welsh sing-song] Now then. You'll be Delphine's lot, is it? She sent a boy ahead with a note. Duw, I've been praying somebody would come, and I'm not a praying man.

[wiping his face] Gethin Pryce, mayor of Dunmere, for my sins. The ore's gone bad — comes up grey and brittle and the smiths won't touch it, and my crews won't go below the second level, and I don't blame them.

q3_tollan_selene_reply.t: [bitter] Same hand, bach, and you know it or you wouldn't ask. The Iron Consortium out of the Gate takes every wagon — they've the roads. They've been very sorry about the bad ore. Very sorry, and very quick to sell the smiths their own stock instead, at a price.

q3_tollan_winston_reply.t: [bitter] One. The Iron Consortium out of the Gate. They've the roads, so they've the ore, and they've been very sorry about it being bad, and very quick to sell the smiths good iron of their own instead.

q3_tollan_ask.t: [hopeful] So. Will you go down, and what will it cost me? Say it plain; I've no head for haggling today.

q3_tollan_crews.t: [low] Lights, on the fourth level, where there's no lamps. Chanting. And a man — the last crew that came up swore it was a man, big, in a robe, standing by something like an altar. They didn't stay to ask him his business, and I don't blame them for that either.

q3_tollan_iron.t: [bitter] Whoever's selling good iron while mine's bad. There's one house doing that on this coast, and it's the Consortium, and I've said so to the magistrate twice and got a shrug both times.

q3_tollan_fee.t: [wincing] Two hundred. There's lovely. — Fine. Fine! Half now and half when you come up, and if you come up with clean ore I'll carry you round the square myself.

q3_tollan_yes.t: [nearly weeping] Bless you. Bless you, I mean it. It won't be much, but it'll be everything we've got, and the whole town will know your name.

q4_thanks.t: [overjoyed] The crews went down at dawn and came up with clean ore. Clean! I haven't heard a bar ring true on that anvil since winter. Duw, I could sing.
[earnest] Dunmere owes you more than it can pay, bach. Here's what it can. And — if you go north after the people who did this, the town would take it kindly if you didn't come back alone.

q4_chamber.t: [hoarse] So. Somebody finally came down. The crews have been whispering about a company from the coast for a week; I hoped you were bringing my pay.
[bitter] They lied about that part. I have not seen a coin since spring. I have letters — orders, names, the whole rotten trade. Let me walk out of this hole and they are yours.

q4_grukhar_winston_reply.t: [hoarse] The Consortium's. They're the ones who hired me. You'll find the details in those letters.

q4_grukhar_who.t: [hoarse] A courier called Femi, who keeps a room at the inn in Thornbury and calls himself a wine merchant. Above him, something that signs itself Gorruk and holds the north road. Above THAT, I never met. Nobody meets it. The money used to come down the same way the orders do.

q4_grukhar_why.t: [a laugh like a cough] You think I asked? Somebody wants iron dear this year. Somebody wants the smiths of the Gate buying from one hand. I was told to keep this mine useless until the spring shipment, and I did, and I was to be paid for it, and I was not.

q4_grukhar_walk.t: [relieved, backing away] The altar. Read the one with the ogre's mark first; it names the courier and the inn.
[muttering] Veylan keep me. I am finished with iron.

q4_grukhar_kill.t: [snarling] Then come and take them, foundling.

q4_chamber_ask.t: [hoarse] Well? The letters for my life. It is a fair trade and you know it.

q5_sage.t: [amused] You have looked at me three times this week, my child, and decided each time that I was nobody. That is a good instinct. It is wrong this once.

[calm] I am called Yohannes. Tesfaye was my friend before this town had a wall, and I have watched his ward from a distance because that is what he asked of me, and because I am a coward about goodbyes.
[quiet, exact] Now. Before I tell you anything, tell me something. The man in black on the Griffon Road. What did he say to Tesfaye? Word for word, if you can.

q5_test_word.t: [very still] "Your library." He knew about the library. Then he has known where you were for years, and waited, and chose his night. That is worse than I feared and better than I guessed: a patient man can be found. — Ask me what you like. I will answer what I can.

q5_test_forget.t: [gently] Then you did as you were told, and you are alive to be asked, and that is the whole of what Tesfaye wanted from that night. Ask me what you like. I will answer what I can.

q5_test_refuse.t: [chuckling] Tesfaye said you would be like this. He said it fondly, mostly. — Ask me what you like, before you go and do it.

q5_torvald_why.t: [gently] He died so that you would live long enough to be told properly, by the right person, in the right place. That place is not a stable yard in Thornbury, and I am not the right person; I am only the one who knew him longest.
[calm] Go north. Find the letters. Paper will bring you to the truth faster than I would, and you will believe paper where you would not believe me.

q5_torvald_armour.t: [carefully] I have not seen his face. I have seen his work. He does not want you dead for anything you have done; he wants you dead for what you are, and he is not the only one who will. That is as much as I will say before you have earned the rest.

q5_torvald_help.t: [dry] I have helped. Twice. You did not see either time, which is what help from me looks like.
[warm] The courier you want keeps a room at the inn here; the bandits are north, in the Gnashing Wood. Bring the letters out alive. That is the help I need from you.

q5_torvald_go.t: [calm] The inn, for the courier. The Gnashing Wood, for the rest. Go well, child, since you will go anyway.

q5_sage_ask.t: [dry] Well? I can see you are not satisfied. Tell me what you want to know.

q5_inn.t: [nervous, city-polished] I do not know you. I do not know any priest, or any mine. I am a wine merchant, my friend, and I should like you to leave my table.

q5_inn_selene_reply.t: [sweating] Ah-ah — madam, I do not answer to — I have a licence, I have papers —

q5_verlan_letters.t: [sweating] Then the priest is a liar. Or dead. Or both. I carry wine. I carry what I am given to carry, and I do not read it, and nobody has ever asked me to.

q5_verlan_pay.t: [greedy, low] Fifty. Yes. There is a map in my boot: past Holloway Vale, under the old oak line. Do not use the road; they watch the road.

q5_inn_ask.t: [stiff] Well? Leave my table, or say what you came to say.

q5_patrol.t: [cold] Yes. Stare. A dark elf, above ground, in daylight. You will not see another.

[contemptuous] I am a priestess, and a fugitive, and there is a bounty on me that these three would like to collect. I cured a village of the coughing sickness on my way here. They are arresting me for having the wrong face. Decide what that makes you.

q5_patrol_cassian_reply.t: [level] Of a goddess your Order has no name for, boy, and would not like if it did. Does it change your sword arm?

q5_ilvara_why.t: [flat] My own people. I refused a thing that was asked of me, and among my kind refusal is answered with a knife. I came up into the light because there was nowhere left to go down. I have not found the light kinder, ya stranger. Only brighter.

q5_ilvara_defend.t: [surprised] Protection. From you. How strange, and how useful.
[dry] Very well. By the deep, I go where you go, until I decide otherwise. Try to be interesting.

q5_ilvara_walk.t: [flat] Of course. Walk on. Everyone does.

q5_ilvara_sell.t: [venomous] You will remember this. I will see that you do, from wherever they put me.

q5_patrol_ask.t: [cold] Well? You have looked long enough to decide.

q9_floor_ilvara.t: [low, amused] Answer her. She is the only person in this tower telling the truth, and she is doing it for money. I respect that.

bond_first.t: [direct] I appreciate what you did for me. Understand something, though. You did not buy my loyalty by keeping me alive.
[firm] I choose where I go and whom I serve.

bond_first_reply.t: [approving] Good. I prefer travelling with someone who understands that.

bond_second.t: [unguarded] I miss the quiet of the shrine. Before the petitions began, I had an hour to myself.
[dry] Up here, someone is always shouting, selling something, or telling me what a lovely morning it is. Usually in the rain.

bond_second_reply.t: [measured] The work was demanding. I liked that. I knew what was expected of me, and I was good at it. I miss having a place of my own.

bond_interest.t: [interested] You have my attention. Let us spend more time together before deciding anything.

bond_later.t: [level] Then leave it for now. You can bring it up when you know what you want.

q9_romance.t: [dry] I enjoy your company when you stop trying to give me orders.
[direct] I would like some time alone with you. Interested?

q9_romance_yes.t: [pleased] Good. Come and sit with me. Your duties can wait for an evening.

q9_romance_no.t: [cool] Very well. I will not ask again.

q10_double_strike.t: [approving] Ruthless. Correct. The real one is breathing behind it; someone drag her out.

q10_double_listen.t: [sharp] That is not your kin. Kill it before it kisses you.

q10_double_strike_alone.t: [approving] Good. You did not even let it finish. There are more behind it; kill them the same way.

q14_sanctum.t: [reverent] Do you feel it? The stone remembers him. Morrak. By the deep — it would remember you too, if you let it.

banter.t: [contemptuous] Bleed, then, if you must.
[cool] Wound them. I will decide who heals.
[dry] Surface-dwellers. Always the front lane.

q5_tent.t: [hoarse, drawling] Visitors. Well, ain't that fine. Y'all here for me, or for the ogre? Say me. Please say me.

[urgent] Cal Boone — Warden, or I was 'fore the chain. That chest by the cot is full of letters, and every last one of 'em carries the same seal. Take the chest. Take me. In that order, if it's got to be.

q5_tent_ithrel_reply.t: [a nod at the cot] Right there, friend. And he's waking up.

q5_letters.t: [grinning through a split lip] Told you. Every one sealed with the iron hand. The Iron Consortium — the trading house in the Gate — pays for the mine, for these bandits, and for you.

[serious] There's a second name under theirs. A mage called Olamide, in the Mirkhollow. They call his place "the other mine." I heard it twice through that tent wall, and men don't say a thing twice unless it matters.

q5_letters_selene_reply.t: [thinking] No name on the paper, Del, I'll swear to that. But the ogre said "the Gate office" like it was one man, and once — only once — "Adeyinka." Said it the way a fella says a name he's scared of.

q5_tent.t: [booming] The foundling. In my own tent. Somebody in the city is going to be very embarrassed when I send them your head in a bag.

q5_escape.t: [snarling] Not today, foundling. Not for you. The city will finish what I started.

q13_again.t: [roaring] YOU. Twice. TWICE you walk into my tent. There is no city to run to this time, orphan.

q6_web.t: [cheerful, from above] Ah — hello. Yes. Up here. In the web. It is exactly as embarrassing as it looks, and I apologise for it.

[appraising] Not bounty hunters; you walk too close together. A green sash — Wardens, then, or with Wardens. Good. Wardens cut people down for nothing. Kaito. I hunt bounties, mostly, and I was hunting a wyvern's head when the spiders took offence.

q6_faelen_wyvern.t: [bright] The magistrate of Thornbury, whose sheep keep disappearing. Three hundred in gold, and — I am told — the gratitude of a woman with a very fine face. I am still negotiating the second part.

q6_faelen_price.t: [delighted] Ah. Now we are talking properly. My bow, until your road ends. And a thing I saw, which I think you will want: east of here, past the wyvern cliffs, there is a mine under the hill. Men in iron livery go in at dawn and men in chains come out at dusk. I did not go closer. I hunt beasts. That did not look like a beast.

q6_faelen_cut.t: [relieved] You are my favourite person. I say that to everyone. This once, forgive me, I mean it.
[smiling] I will come along, if you will have me. The wyverns are that way, and so, I suspect, is whatever you came into these woods to find.

q6_faelen_leave.t: [calling after you] Fair enough! If you change your mind, I will be — well. Here.

q6_wyverns.t: [bright] There she is. The matriarch. That head is worth three hundred in gold and a magistrate's gratitude, and I intend, respectfully, to collect both.

q8_door.t: [murmuring] Doorman. Big. Bored. I can talk us past him; bored men love a story, and I have several.

q8_door_faelen.t: [pleased] — and that is how I lost the boot. He is still laughing. In, in, before he thinks about it.

q8_door_force.t: [resigned] Through him. Very well. I will apologise to him afterwards; it seems only polite.

q9_lobby.t: [murmuring] A clerk. A list. Two guards. Forgive me — I love a lobby.

q9_lobby_talk.t: [smiling] He believed it. Third floor. Touch nothing, he says — as if.

bond_first.t: [quieter] I know I make a performance of everything. It is easier than admitting I was scared.
[honest] When you found me, I thought I was going to die there. I have been sleeping badly since.

bond_first_reply.t: [soft] Thank you. I might be rather poor company tonight, but I would like you to stay.

bond_second.t: [cheerful] I used to play for supper at roadside inns. I know six songs well and about forty badly.
[smiling] I still have the lute. I sold the feathered hat. A man has to improve himself somehow.

bond_second_reply.t: [amused] Cruel, but fair. I will play you the good six. You can request the others after enough wine.

bond_interest.t: [pleased] I was hoping you might say that. Let us have a little time together and see how we get on.

bond_later.t: [easy] All right. Let me know if you want to try again. No awkwardness between us.

q9_romance.t: [smiling] I like you. I'd like to spend an evening with you, without the rest of this lot.

q9_romance_yes.t: [delighted] Excellent. A decent meal, some wine, and no work.
[warm] I have been looking forward to this.

q9_romance_no.t: [light] Stop it is. Friends, then, and I am very good at that as well.

q10_double_strike.t: [wincing] Right call, wrong result — the real Hiwot was behind it. She is breathing. I will carry her out; go.

q10_double_strike_alone.t: [breathless] Not him — and you knew. It is down. Two more behind it, and I do not like their faces either.

q10_double_listen.t: [shouting] Not them! NOT them! It has teeth, {target}!

q13_maze.t: [hushed] The thieves' maze. Every third flagstone is a trap and every fourth is a thief. I know the path; follow my feet exactly, please.

q13_maze_follow.t: [murmuring] Left. Left. Do not step there. — And we are through, and nobody even bled. I love being right.

q13_maze_cut.t: [sighing] Straight through. Watch the flagstones, then, and try to bleed on the thieves and not on me.

banter.t: [smiling] Loosing, loosing — got him, and he was handsome, too. A pity.
[cheerful] Behind them! I am behind them!
[light] If I die, tell the magistrate I was thinking of her.

q6_grove.t: [fierce] Far enough. This wood is not a road, and you are not welcome on it. The Umbra hold this grove, and the Umbra say turn around. Eh?
[sniffing] You carry iron from the Gate. The wood smells it on you. Which of you is theirs?

q6_grove_selene_reply.t: [narrowing] A Warden says so. Wardens said so about the last mine, and the last mine is still there.
[low] Mzee Kamau would sooner have you bleed than speak. I would sooner hear you first. So. Speak.

q6_grove_ask.t: [low] No answer. Then hear this: the Mzee would sooner have you bleed than speak. I would sooner hear you first. Speak, or turn around.

q6_nettle_ask.t: [bitter] Dead fish for a mile downstream. Stags with sores on their flanks. And men — men in chains, walking into a hole in the hill every dawn, and fewer walking out. The wood knows what is being done to it. It does not know how to stop it. I do.

q6_nettle_talk.t: [grudging] Then we want the same thing, and I would rather kill them beside you than argue with the Mzee about killing you.
[decisive] Sawa. I am coming. He can take it up with the trees.

q6_nettle_fight.t: [snarling] Then the roots will have you. MZEE! Kamau! They have chosen!

q7_mine_umbra.t: [hard] For two years, I have watched the river get worse. Dead fish, sick animals. All because of this place.
[firm] I want this mine shut before we leave.

banter.t: [snarling] The roots have him.
[fierce] Trees do not forgive. Neither do I.
[low] Bleed into the soil. Good. Sawa.

q6_grove_mzee.t: [old, unhurried] Wanjiru. They have been told to leave.
[flat] I have buried nine of ours since that mine opened. If these people work for the Consortium, they will get no mercy from me.
[cold] Hear them out if you must. They stay where they are.

q6_grove_mzee_peace.t: [flat, from the trees] Wanjiru. If they are lying, you are the one who let them in.
[grudging] Go with them, then. Make sure they shut that mine. I expect you back when it is done.

q7_cage.t: [gravelly, Welsh] Well now. Either you're the new drivers or the old ones are dead. Which is it, then? — No, don't tell me; you're too muddy for drivers, and they'd have shot me by now.

[hopeful] Dai Morgan. Priest of the deep places, and the last of the clan that cut this mine before the Consortium took it with paper and knives. I know every valve in it — including the one at the bottom that lets the river in.

q7_cage_beau_reply.t: [grim] Bottom level, by the valve room, so the drivers can drown them if the mine's ever taken. Mind that, shield-man. Whoever turns that wheel turns it on them.

q7_durnik_paper.t: [grim] A debt we didn't owe, bought off a man who didn't own it, and enforced by men with swords while the magistrate looked at the ceiling. My cousins argued. My cousins are on the lowest level now, and they don't argue anymore.

q7_durnik_free.t: [grunting to his feet] With you. Aye. There's lovely. Mind the third level; the mage keeps his study there, and he doesn't care for knocking.

q7_durnik_leave.t: [flat] Come back for me. Aye. Everybody says that, bach.

q7_study_dai.t: [very level] Morgan. Bryn and Gareth Morgan. My cousins. Which ledger are they in, mage?

q7_study_dai_after.t: [quiet] ...Then I'll be having ledger four. Go on, {target}.

q7_valve.t: [urgent] The valve room. Turn the great wheel and the river takes the bottom two levels in the time it takes to say a prayer.
[hard] Your shield-man went below for the chain-gang. He isn't up yet.

q7_cage_ask.t: [hopeful] So. Are you letting me out, or are you the polite sort of drivers?

q8_sewers.t: [approving] Good stonework, mind. Dwarven, some of it, and old. Shame about the smell.

q9_lobby.t: [gravelly] Clerk with a list. Two guards. Good stone, again. Shame.

q9_lobby_talk.t: [grunting] Third floor. Don't touch anything. Good advice for a tower, that.

banter.t: [gravelly] Wall. I'm the wall, I am.
[grunting] Hit 'em. I've got 'em.
[calm] The deep places keep me. Keep going, bach.

q7_study.t: [irritated] Get away from my desk. Those ledgers are Consortium property.
[cold] Guards, kill them. The Consortium wants this mine kept running.

q7_study_dai_reply.t: [without looking up] Ledger four. The deceased column, I should think; the deep levels take the dwarves first. Guards!

q7_study_winston_reply.t: [contemptuous] Both. One to each partner, and neither to you. Guards!

q7_malvane_who.t: [contemptuous] To the Gate office, and the Gate office answers to the men whose names are on the letters you have not yet found. You will not find them, my friend. Guards!

q7_study_ask.t: [cold] Well? You have interrupted my afternoon. Say why.

q8_span.t: [gruff] Serpent's Span. Papers. — Ah. You are the company from the south. The one that drowned the Consortium's mine; half the city has heard it, the Consortium made sure of that when they went crying to the Council.
[plain] Emeka Obi, Burning Gauntlet. One question before anything, and I want a number, not a story. The Consortium told the Council there were no slaves in that mine. How many did you see in chains?

q8_count_nineteen.t: [writing] Nineteen. Good. A number a man can read aloud to a room of merchants. I will remember it when they tell me again that there were none.

q8_count_many.t: [grunting] Cages. Ah-ah. "Cages" is a word the Council can argue with; a number they cannot. Next time, count. — It is not a small thing, what you did down there. I will say that once.

q8_count_none.t: [flat] Between you and the Duke. Very well. The Duke will ask the same question, and he does not like "between" any more than I do.

q8_jobs.t: [plain] Duke Adebayo wants a word with you, but first I want two things done, and I would rather they were done by people the Consortium already hates. One: something under the docks is eating dock-workers, and the sewer-men will not go down. Two: the Nine Lanterns trading house has stopped being the Nine Lanterns. Same faces, wrong people; I cannot explain it better than that, and I have tried.

q8_halloran_why.t: [quiet] Because the iron trouble has a name now, and the name is the Iron Consortium, and you are the only people alive who walked out of their mine with proof. He does not know you. He knows that. Do the jobs, my friend. Bring the proof.

q8_halloran_yes.t: [approving] Good answer. The docks are that way. Hold your breath.

q8_halloran_pay.t: [snorting] It pays. Not well. Nobody in this city pays well except the people you are fighting.

q8_duke.t: [weary] So. The company that drowned a mine. Obi says you are rude and effective. I have use for both.
[precise] Before I say anything worth hearing: the papers you carried out of that mine. Who else has seen them? Every name. I do not enjoy surprises in Council.

q8_seen_nobody.t: [a nod] Good. Keep it so. A paper nobody has read is worth twice one everybody has argued about.

q8_seen_hand.t: [a long breath] The Umbral Hand. Then the whole market will have read them by the week's end, and the Council will hear it from fishwives before it hears it from me. Ah-ah. — Fine. Faster than my clerks, at least. It is not a small thing you have done, and I am not yet sure whether it was a good one.

q8_seen_wardens.t: [dry] Wardens. Then they are honest and nobody in this city will believe them. Good. That is one problem I already know how to solve.

q8_duke_work.t: [precise] The Consortium poisoned its rivals' ore and kept its own iron to sell at a higher price. Adigun blames Calder for the shortage. Now someone is demanding we settle it with a war. The Council votes in a fortnight. I need the orders from their tower to prove who caused this, before ten thousand people die over a shortage those men arranged.

q8_halvard_city.t: [nodding] Good. I will remember that when this is over. Dukes remember more than people think, my friend.

q8_halvard_pay.t: [dry] Five hundred on delivery. Obi will scowl. Ignore him; he scowls at me too.

q8_halvard_blood.t: [careful] I do not know, and I will not insult you with a guess. I know they were hunting Tesfaye's ward before they were hunting anyone else, and Tesfaye was a Warden who spent twenty years hiding something in a library.
[quiet] Bring me the papers. Whatever they are hiding, it will be in them.

q9_plan.t: [precise] The Consortium is hiring swords. Go in as hired guards and search the top-floor offices. We need the orders bearing Adigun's seal.
[dry] If you can do it without burning the tower down, the city would appreciate it. If you cannot, the city will understand.

q9_book.t: [grave] The keepers hold shipping records both kingdoms trust. They are hearing the dispute over the iron shortage. Take Adigun's orders to Lanternhold and show them who caused it.
[quiet] I will have my officers keep looking for Kolade here. His father may know where he is. Question Adigun, and bring him back alive if you can. This book will pay your way into the keep.

q11_cured.t: [weak] Poison. Slow. He was — the physician was — I could not make my mouth work to say it.
[rallying] Kolade. It was always Kolade. Get me to my own guard and I will get you into that coronation.

q11_way.t: [stronger] Two invitations and a Duke who owes you his life. Olumide will hold the doors. Folasade will hold the Council. You hold the evidence.
[grave] He will not go quietly. He will run for the Undercity. When he does, do not let him reach the altar first.

q12_council_dead.t: [hoarse, from a chair] Two Grand Dukes dead in their own hall, and the Council is me and a room full of ghosts. It is not a small thing you did, running at him.
[hard] The vote is dead with them; nobody will vote for his war now. Go down and finish it. I will hold what is left.

q9_tower.t: [quiet, city-formal] Tesfaye's ward. I am Sanni. I knew him through the keep's book trade. He wrote about you and Hiwot. I was sorry to hear what happened on the Griffon Road.

[low] Adigun Adeyinka is my father. Those orders from the mine carry his seal. He and his partners have gone to Lanternhold for a hearing over the iron shortage. He means to persuade the keepers that Calder is to blame.

[urgent] He is preparing a war with Calder. Kill him before he buys the Council's vote and you could save thousands of lives. Go to the summit at Lanternhold. Read the evidence first, and hear what he has to say. I will meet you there.

q10_ring.t: [quiet, city-formal] You found the papers, then. My father is in the reading room with Bankole and Rotimi. Before you go in, I have something of Tesfaye's for you.
[calm] Take this ring. It was his once, before it was mine. And know this, my friend: the three men inside deserve whatever you decide to give them. Nobody will weep.

q10_ring_hiwot_reply.t: [a warm, easy smile] He had dealings outside the keep, young lady. Some of them were confidential. I gave him my word that they would stay that way.

q10_ring_hiwot_end.t: [pleasantly] No. It is not. — The ring, {target}. Take it or do not; I have a long walk either way.

q10_sarn_take.t: [soft] Wear it inside. The keepers will know it. Find my father before he leaves the reading room.

q10_sarn_refuse.t: [amused] Wise. Tesfaye taught you that. Go well anyway.

q10_sarn_threat.t: [pleased] I believe you would. Go well, {target}.

q10_murder.t: [cold] You were supposed to kill him. Very well. Father, your couriers brought me your letter to the Council. You will not be calling off my war.

q10_accuse.t: [shouting] Guards! In here! Tesfaye's ward has murdered my father and his partners. Take their weapons. Do not let this company leave the keep!

q10_ring_ask.t: [pleasantly] Take it or do not, my friend; I have a long walk either way.

q9_floor.t: [silken] Put the swords down; you will not need them on my floor, and I have poured two cups. I am Folake. I keep Kolade Adeyinka's bed warm and the Consortium's secrets warmer.
[pleasant] I have given you his name. Now tell me what happened on the Griffon Road. Before Tesfaye died, did Kolade offer him a bargain? He usually does. I want to know what he offered.

q9_offer_library.t: [satisfied] His library. Not gold, not the child's life — the old man's books. Kolade knew what Tesfaye loved and offered him exactly that. That is how he does everything, my dear, and it is why he will win unless somebody who understands him is on the other side. Which brings us to business.

q9_offer_nothing.t: [a small smile] A lie, and a loyal one. He offered. He always offers; it is the only thing about him I still find beautiful. Keep your lie; it tells me you loved the old man, which is also useful. Now, business.

q9_offer_price.t: [delighted] Oh, good. Somebody taught you. — I am selling a way into the palace, and the truth about what you are, and I want his head and the Consortium afterward. That is the whole shop. Now you know the price; pay me the answer, or do not, and we go on to business either way.

q9_lysandra_kolade.t: [precise] Adigun Adeyinka's foster-son, and the head of the Consortium in everything but the ledger. The man in the black armour on your road; he told me about the road himself, and he told it fondly. He collects people like you. He says you are family. He does not mean it kindly, and he does not mean it as a threat either, which is the frightening part.

q9_lysandra_deal.t: [pleased] Adigun wants high iron prices. A frightened city pays them. Kolade wants the war to happen. He has been using his father's couriers to hunt Morrak's children behind his back, and his tutor promises him godhood through mass murder. His father would stop the war if he knew how close it was.
[soft] When you need a way into the palace, come to me. I will have one. The price is his head, and the Consortium afterward — for me.

q9_lysandra_arrest.t: [amused] Chains. How lawful. Fine. I will tell Adebayo everything and he will hang me for it, and Kolade will still be sworn in on time.
[bitter] Go upstairs. The top floor is where he keeps the truth about you.

q9_lysandra_kill.t: [whispering] He will feel this. That is the only thing I am sorry for.

q9_floor_wait.t: [patient, smiling] I can wait. I am very good at waiting; it is most of what I do up here.

q9_floor_business.t: [brisk, pleasant] Now. He is going to be a Grand Duke by month's end, and he is going to have you killed for it. I would rather the reverse. Shall we talk, my dear?

q11_way.t: [silken] Two invitations and a bargain kept. His head; my Consortium. I will have a carriage at the palace steps.
[cool] When it goes wrong — and it will — he will run for the Undercity. I will show you the way down. Nobody else knows it but Amara.

q12_council_dead.t: [cool] Two dead dukes. You do not do things by halves, my dear; I will remember that when I am counting what is left of the Council.
[silken] The carriage is at the steps. The way down is under the palace kitchens. Bring me his head.

q13_trust.t: [quiet] You kept your word. Thank you for letting me help.

q11_docks.t: [steady] Put the swords away. If I wanted you dead I would have done it from the rooftop.

[grave] I am Amara. I love Kolade Adeyinka. I also helped him kill the man who raised you. I know what that makes me to you. But I need you to hear me. Have you ever loved someone even after you knew what they'd done?

q11_loved_yes.t: [a slow nod] Then you know the shape of it. Good. I will not have to explain the rest, only ask it.

q11_loved_tesfaye.t: [quiet] Yes. Kolade has lied to me too. I know he has hurt people. I still care for him, but I cannot let him go on killing.

q11_loved_no.t: [level] Then you will think what I ask is weakness. Hear it anyway; you may need it later, when you are older and less certain.

q11_docks_ithrel_reply.t: [without flinching] No. I was not. But I did not stop him sending Gorruk north, and I could have. Put that on my account with the rest, ranger. I will not argue the sum.

q11_docks_ask.t: [grave] Here is what I ask. Stop him. Not kill him. Stop him. There is a difference, and it matters to me more than my own life.

q11_amara_how.t: [exact] Chains, and a cell, and the Council's law. He is not a god yet. He bleeds, he tires, he can be beaten to his knees; I have seen it done, once, in the fire temple where we met. On his knees he can be bound. It is not a small thing I ask. I know that.

q11_amara_promise.t: [exhaling] Thank you. I did not expect that.
[quiet] The coronation is in three nights. Two people called Rasheed and Kemi hold the invitations in the Undervault. Take them from them; they will not give them up.

q11_amara_refuse.t: [cold] Then we will meet at the gate of the Undercity, and one of us will not walk past the other.
[flat] Rasheed and Kemi hold the invitations. Undervault. Take them; it does not change what I said.

q11_amara_lie.t: [searching] ...Your word. Yes. — Rasheed and Kemi, the Undervault. The invitations. Go.

q13_gate.t: [quiet] I said one of us would not walk past the other.
[steady] I am still asking. Stop him. Do not kill him. And if you cannot promise me that, then draw, because I will not let you reach him without it.

q13_gate_pass.t: [stepping aside] Go. I will be at the altar before you, on my knees, asking him the same thing. He will not listen to me. He might listen to you.

q13_gate_join.t: [startled] With — yes. Yes. I know the way; I have walked it a hundred times. Stay behind me at the stairs.

q13_gate_lie.t: [searching your face] ...Go, then. If you are lying, I will know it at the altar.

q14_plea.t: [kneeling] Kolade. Please. Look at me. It does not have to be the altar. It can be a cell and a window and me visiting every week for the rest of your life.

banter.t: [exact] Two blades. Two throats. Next.
[steady] Watch the flank. I have the front.
[quiet] Not like this. Quickly. Clean.

q10_gate.t: [cold] A book buys you the door. It does not buy you my good opinion.
[stiff] Where did he die? On what road, and on what night? The keep's book of the dead wants a road and a night, and nobody has given me either.

q10_where_road.t: [writing, not looking up] "The Griffon Road. Standing." — Tesfaye left this keep with you and came back to it as a line in my book. Do not make a habit of it.

q10_where_refuse.t: [cold] "On the road." Very well. It is what he would have wanted written; he never cared for particulars. Do not make a habit of this, child.

q10_arrest.t: [thundering] Three men dead in my reading room. Put down your weapons. You and your whole company are under arrest. To the cells. Now.

q10_arrest_spared.t: [thundering] You say you spared them. Sanni says he found you over their bodies. I will hear you separately, under guard. Put down your weapons. To the cells.

q10_gate.t: [kind] Pay him no mind. He mourns like a wall. — Come and find me in the upper reading room before you do anything else, my child. Tesfaye left something with me. For you. For now.

q10_letter.t: [gently] Sit. I have Tesfaye's letter here. Before you read it... did he say anything at the end? I need to know.

q10_end_proud.t: [closing his eyes] Then he managed it. He practised that sentence on me for a year, my child, and never once got through it without stopping. — Here. Read it. I will stay.

q10_end_run.t: [softly] "Run." Yes. He was a practical man to the last breath. He wrote the rest down, so that he would not have to trust the last breath to carry it. — Here. Read it. I will stay.

q10_end_nothing.t: [gently] Then you did the only thing he asked, and it is the reason I can give you this at all. — Here. Read it. I will stay.

q10_letter_give.t: [quiet] Tesfaye began this letter when he brought you here. He added to it before you left. He asked me to keep it safe until you were ready to know.

q10_letter_grief.t: [soft] He raised a child. What the child became was always going to be the child's own work. He knew that. He hoped.

q10_letter_anger.t: [sad] He tried, every year. He wrote it out and burned it. He thought one more year of not knowing was one more year of you being only his.

q10_letter_hunger.t: [frightened] Do not — {target}. He wrote the last line for exactly that look on your face. Read it again.

q10_escape.t: [urgent] I brought the cell key. Your gear is in the chest outside; take it. Sanni has ordered your transfer to the Gate at dawn. I do not trust him. The old passage behind this wall leads through the catacombs to the shore. Go, and do not trust any face you meet down there.

q10_summit.t: [startled] Guards — no. No, hold. I know who you are.

[shaking] Adigun Adeyinka. The mines, the bandits, the lies about Calder — we paid for those. I wanted higher prices, not a war that would close our trade routes. My foster-son is buying votes to send the army across the border. He used my seal to order your death, and Tesfaye's. My own couriers obey him now.

q10_summit_selene_reply.t: [miserable] Mine. The house's. — He took it off my desk in the spring, and my couriers with it, and I have been signing for a man who no longer asks me.

q10_summit_kill.t: [terrified] He will not stop when we are dead. He will not STOP —

q10_summit_talk.t: [whispering] Kolade. Kolade Adeyinka. His tutor told him who his real father was. Then he started paying for reports on other children, all over the coast. I thought he was looking for relatives. I found the death notices with the bounty payments.
[broken] He is in this keep tonight. I do not know what face he is wearing.

q10_summit_arrest.t: [relieved] Yes. Yes. Adebayo. Anything. Take us out of here before he —

q10_summit.t: [bluster] Kill them, Adigun, they have swords in a LIBRARY —

q10_catacombs.t: [bored] Down here, then. Good. Fewer witnesses and no keepers.
[professional] Gbenga. Your brother sends his regards and would like this finished before breakfast. — Which of you is the ward? I was given a face, not a name, and it is dark.

q10_catacombs_end.t: [sighing] Then all of you. It costs me nothing extra.

q10_unmasked.t: [dry] Your father is dead, Kolade. The ward has escaped the keep. I take it we are continuing with the war?

q12_teleport.t: [dry] My boy. This way. — You people: enjoy the rear-guard. They were expensive, o.

q11_healer.t: [oily] The Duke is resting. He must not be disturbed. I am his physician, and I will thank you to —
[dropping the voice] — ah. You. The face on the posters. How very tiresome.

q11_undervault.t: [grinning] Kemi. Kemi, look. It is the poster. In person! Ah-ah — do we get the reward if we kill it ourselves?
[bored] The reward is a thousand and the invitations are worth more. Stop talking and start bleeding them.

q11_way.t: [soft] Two invitations, and a debt to the Undervault that you will pay when I say. Fair?
[softer] Fair. Here is what nobody told you, my friend: under the palace is the old city. Under the old city is a temple. He is going there when it falls apart. So are you.

q12_council_dead.t: [soft] Two dead dukes and a hall full of witnesses. The Undervault will take you down; the Gauntlet is too busy counting bodies.
[softer] The debt grows, {target}. It always does.

q12_hall.t: [booming] Blades! Blades in the hall! Folasade — Folasade, to me —

q12_dukes_orlan.t: [roaring] HA! With me, then! Folasade — Folasade, get BEHIND something!

q12_council.t: [wheezing] Folasade is dead. He put a knife in her while the whole hall watched.
[grim] The vote is dead too; she made sure of that first. Go and finish him. I will hold the door until you come back or he does.

q12_dukes_mira.t: [sharp] Good. Keep them off me and I will keep the Council listening. That is the only thing that matters in this room.

q12_council.t: [shaken] The Council has read it. The vote on the war is dead, and so is his claim.
[steady] He went into the ground. Olumide is bleeding but standing. Go and finish it, and bring me a head or a prisoner; I will take either.

q13_street.t: [sneering] The brother. Or the sister. It does not matter which — Kolade says the blood is the same, and the blood is what burns.

q13_steps.t: [sneering] The Gauntlet stands with the new Duke. Whatever is left of the Council can argue about it afterwards.
[cold] I signed your poster myself, my friend. Let me sign the rest of it.

q13_steps_selene_reply.t: [cold] In the river, where the old Duke's friends go. Tell her to look downstream.

wren_ward.name: Hiwot
wren_ward.desc: Your foster-sister from Lanternhold, raised beside you in the keepers' library. Quick hands, quicker mouth, hides fear behind jokes.

dorran.name: Beau
dorran.desc: A Warden fighter from the Shore Road with a stammer he hates and a shield he never puts down. Delphine's husband.

selene.name: Delphine
selene.desc: Beau's wife and an old friend of your late stepfather, Tesfaye. She regards you as family. A Warden druid of the Shore Road: blunt, protective, allergic to self-pity. Speaks for the balance of things.

vess.name: Desmond
vess.desc: An Umbral Hand necromancer who giggles at wounds. Unstable, brilliant, always listening for the Hand.

fennick.name: Winston
fennick.desc: Desmond's halfling minder. Sour, practical, would sell you for a good boot. Umbral Hand.

cassian.name: Santiago
cassian.desc: A squire of the Order of the Dawning Flame, from its chapter house in the sun-lands, on his first errand. Earnest, rigid, secretly terrified of failing.

ithrel.name: Itsuki
ithrel.desc: An elf ranger of the eastern woods who has hunted the bandit lord Gorruk for a year. Grief made him quiet; the quiet made him precise.

bramm.name: Bahadır
bramm.desc: A huge, loud ranger of Kalden who travels with a tiger named Fındık. Fiercely loyal to Yasemin and his company.

ysolde.name: Yasemin
ysolde.desc: A Kalden witch under Bahadır's guard. Formal, watchful, sees the bloodline in you before you do.

aurelius.name: Devendra
aurelius.desc: A Crimson Wizard of Vashk who narrates his own superiority under his breath. Wants Yasemin dead; wants you useful.

ilvara.name: Layla
ilvara.desc: A dark-elf priestess of the deep cities, fleeing her own people and a bounty. Contemptuous, curious, thinks mercy is a luxury the strong buy.

faelen.name: Kaito
faelen.desc: An elf bounty-hunter of the eastern woods who flirts with anything and finishes every job. Cheerful, mercenary, surprisingly loyal.

nettle.name: Wanjiru
nettle.desc: An Umbra druid of the Mirkhollow who believes the forest is owed blood. Fierce, literal, no patience for cities.

durnik.name: Dai Morgan
durnik.desc: A dwarf priest whose clan dug the Mirkhollow mine before the Consortium stole it. Slow to anger, impossible to move.

amara.name: Amara
amara.desc: Kolade's lover and sword-hand. A monk of the Gate's fire temples who wants him stopped, not slaughtered. Grave, exact, tired.

aldric.name: Tesfaye
aldric.desc: Your foster-father, a retired Warden mage who keeps the library at Lanternhold. Gentle voice, iron patience, a man who has planned for this night for twenty years.

torvald.name: Yohannes
torvald.desc: The sage in the grey cloak, a hill-man of the old highland school. Old beyond reason, amused by everything, tells you exactly as much as he decides you can carry.

tollan.name: Gethin Pryce
tollan.desc: Mayor of Dunmere. Sweating, harried, honest enough. Would pay anyone to make the mine problem someone else's.

halloran.name: Emeka Obi
halloran.desc: A Burning Gauntlet officer with a burn-scarred jaw. Plain-spoken, fair, dead by the eleventh chapter.

halvard.name: Duke Adebayo
halvard.desc: Grand Duke and commander of the Burning Gauntlet. Tired, precise, poisoned by the end.

orlan.name: Duke Olumide
orlan.desc: A Grand Duke who was a soldier first and still stands like one. Loud, decent, easily bored.

mira.name: Duke Folasade
mira.desc: A Grand Duke and a mage. Watches everyone, trusts nobody, and is usually right.

ambrose.name: Dawit
ambrose.desc: A keeper of Lanternhold and Tesfaye's friend. Kind eyes, careful hands, keeps the letter you were never supposed to read.

hadrian.name: Abba Gebre
hadrian.desc: First Keeper of Lanternhold. Proud of the library and suspicious of everyone who leaves it, you most of all.

cael.name: Cal Boone
cael.desc: A Warden spy from the Shore Road who was caught. Half-starved, still joking, remembers every name he heard in the tent.

fen.name: Tunde Softfoot
fen.desc: The thieves' guild's voice in the Undervault. Soft-spoken, keeps ledgers of favours, never forgets a debt.

lysandra.name: Folake
lysandra.desc: Kolade's mistress and the Consortium's cleverest survivor. Silk voice, ledger heart, offers a deal in every sentence.

ostwin.name: Baba Olusegun
ostwin.desc: Kolade's tutor in the old prophecies. Dry, doting, the only one who calls Kolade 'my boy'.

sarn.name: Sanni
sarn.desc: Sanni, a courteous merchant who claims to know Tesfaye and steers the ward against Adigun. Kolade's civilian identity, used to engineer the murder and arrest.

nib.name: Nib
nib.desc: The first hired knife, a Shore Road man in a road-cloak with a purse to earn. Easy-going about murder; not paid enough to be brave.

korvath.name: Kolade Adeyinka
korvath.desc: Your half-brother, raised in the Gate by a Consortium merchant. A giant in spiked black plate who believes bloodshed is a ladder. Calm, courteous, absolutely certain.

morwin.name: Merle
morwin.desc: A hired mage-assassin from the Thornbury country with a bounty notice in his coat. Talks too much before he casts.

lessa.name: Lurleen
lessa.desc: A knife for hire from the Shore Road who takes her work personally. Smiles when she is losing.

verlan.name: Femi
verlan.desc: The Consortium's courier in Thornbury, a city man posing as a wine merchant. Sweats when questioned, folds when paid.

grukhar.name: Grukhar
grukhar.desc: A half-orc priest of Veylan poisoning the Dunmere ore for pay he has not been paid. Bitter, frightened, dangerous.

gorruk.name: Gorruk
gorruk.desc: An ogre-mage who runs the bandit companies for the Consortium. Cruel for sport, cowardly when it counts.

thornwise.name: Mzee Kamau
thornwise.desc: The Umbra archdruid of the Mirkhollow. Believes every axe-holder deserves a root through the chest.

malvane.name: Olamide
malvane.desc: The Consortium mage running the Mirkhollow mine. Fussy, meticulous, keeps the slaves' names in a ledger.

grell.name: Gbenga
grell.desc: Kolade's best knife, sent into the catacombs to finish it. Professional, bored, unbothered by tombs.

idris.name: Idris
idris.desc: The 'healer' at Duke Adebayo's bedside. A doppelganger wearing a physician.

ravel.name: Rasheed
ravel.desc: Half of Kolade's pet assassins. Loud, vain, deadly with two blades.

kessa.name: Kemi
kessa.desc: The other half. Quiet, a mage, the one who actually plans.

jarem.name: Jelani
jarem.desc: Kolade's court mage. Serves because Kolade is winning; would serve anyone who was.

lucan.name: Segun Marr
lucan.desc: The Burning Gauntlet officer who sold the company to Kolade. Commands it now. Sneers to hide the shame.

maddox.name: Adigun Adeyinka
maddox.desc: Head of the Iron Consortium's Gate office and Kolade's foster-father. A merchant who thinks he is still in charge.

vask.name: Bankole
vask.desc: A Consortium leader; Adigun's partner. Louder than he is clever.

rennick.name: Rotimi
rennick.desc: A Consortium leader; the accountant. Would like to survive this meeting.

hero.title: The Gate Stands
hero.line: You stopped Kolade and prevented the war.

monster.title: A Dangerous Inheritance
monster.line: Kolade is dead. Morrak's power remains within you.

usurper.title: The Throne Claimed
usurper.line: You defeated Kolade and took the throne for yourself.

mercy.title: Kolade in Chains
mercy.line: You brought him back alive to answer for his crimes.

ascetic.title: An Unfinished Reckoning
ascetic.line: You refused the throne and left Kolade alive.

restored.title: Home Together
restored.line: You gave up the throne to bring Hiwot home.

ascended.title: Morrak’s Successor
ascended.line: You claimed the throne. Hiwot did not return.

ending.mercy: Kolade Adeyinka was imprisoned beneath the Gauntlet's hall. The Consortium's ledgers were made public, and the Council rejected war with Calder. You had stopped him without killing him. He would face trial for the people he had ordered murdered.

She woke beside you on the temple floor, alive and mortal. The passage closed behind you. You had lost your claim to the throne, but you could take your sister home.

allegiance.gauntlet: Duke Adebayo recovered and kept his promise to you. The wanted posters came down, and the Gauntlet publicly cleared your company's name. Its hall recorded your part in exposing Kolade.
allegiance.consortium: Folake took control of the Consortium and honored her bargain with you. She began reopening trade routes and hiring new guards. Her letters made it clear that she hoped to employ you again.
allegiance.thieves: Tunde Softfoot had given you a way into the palace when you needed one. Afterwards, he reminded you that the favor had not been a gift. He had yet to name his price.
allegiance.none: The Council publicly cleared your name and thanked you for exposing the conspiracy. You left without entering the service of any of the city's factions.

dukes.both: Olumide and Folasade survived the attack on the Council. Together, they began restoring order and investigating the officials Kolade had paid.
dukes.one: Folasade was buried with the city's honors. Olumide survived, but the attack left the Council badly weakened.
dukes.none: Olumide and Folasade were buried on the same morning. Their deaths left the surviving councillors to choose new leaders and settle a frightened city.

wren_ward.present: Hiwot opened a small locksmith's shop on the harbour road. She repaired locks by day and declined to explain where she had learned to open the difficult ones.
wren_ward.gone: Hiwot returned to Lanternhold. Brother Yonas listened to her account of the journey, then asked her to write it down for the archives.

dorran.present: Beau helped the people driven from their homes by the fighting. When there was heavy work to do, he was usually the first to volunteer. He never had much patience for being called a hero.
dorran.dead: Beau's companions raised a memorial for him near Mirkhollow. They remembered his loyalty, his patience, and how readily he had put himself in danger for others.

selene.present: Delphine helped rebuild the Warden house on the Shore Road. She kept Tesfaye's letters there, along with a room you could use whenever you visited.
selene.gone: Delphine returned to the Wardens. News of the campaign reached her through their reports.

vess.present: Desmond stayed in Varenholm and found work trading information. He was careful about who knew his clients' names.
vess.gone: No reliable news of Desmond reached you after Kolade's defeat. The Umbral Hand refused to discuss its agents.

fennick.present: Winston took work guarding merchant caravans. He insisted on seeing the route, the cargo and the full payment before agreeing to leave town.
fennick.gone: No further word of Winston reached you after Kolade's defeat.

cassian.present: Santiago was knighted by the Order of the Dawning Flame. His report named the companions who had helped him, including those his superiors would rather have left out.
cassian.gone: Santiago returned to the Order of the Dawning Flame. He sent occasional letters, keeping his account of the journey brief.

ithrel.present: Itsuki visited his wife's grave before settling outside the city. He began taking work as a guide again, and made plans that had nothing to do with revenge.
ithrel.gone: Itsuki travelled north after leaving the company. Little news of him reached Varenholm.

bramm.present: Bahadır settled by the river with Fındık. The tiger liked to sleep across the front steps. Visitors soon learned to call from the gate.

ysolde.present: Yasemin stayed in Varenholm to continue her studies. She kept in touch with the people who had helped free her.

aurelius.present: Devendra returned to Vashk and secured a promotion from the Crimson Wizards. He sent you a copy of his report. Your name appeared in it, though not nearly as often as his.

ilvara.present: Layla opened a small chapel in Varenholm. People who would once have crossed the street to avoid her began coming to her for healing. She made them wait their turn like everyone else.
ilvara.gone: Layla left Varenholm after the fighting ended. She gave no destination and made no promise to return.

faelen.present: Kaito found steady work as a tracker. Between jobs, he performed in the inns. He asked you not to mention the spiders during his songs about the campaign.
faelen.gone: Kaito returned to the inns of Thornbury. His songs about the campaign gave him a considerably larger role than you remembered.

nettle.present: Wanjiru returned to Mirkhollow to help restore the riverbanks and woodland damaged by the mine. She had little interest in the celebrations in Varenholm; she wanted to see the river run clear again.
nettle.gone: Wanjiru returned to Mirkhollow after leaving your company. She sent word that the river was beginning to clear.

durnik.present: Dai Morgan obtained permission to reclaim his clan's mine. Before work began, he made copies of the prisoners' names and arranged a memorial for those who had died there.
durnik.gone: Dai Morgan left the company to seek help reclaiming his clan's mine.

amara.present: Amara visited Kolade in prison. She still cared for him, but no longer excused what he had done.
amara.gone: Amara left Varenholm by sea. She asked for privacy and gave no address where she could be reached.
amara.dead: Amara was buried near the entrance to the Undercity, where she had tried to stop you from reaching Kolade.

cassian.line: Santiago asked you to attend his knighting. You went together, then slipped away for supper before the speeches had finished.
cassian.favoured: He asked to help rebuild the damaged streets. You spent several mornings working beside him.

ithrel.line: You and Itsuki make time to walk outside the city. Some days he speaks about his wife. On others, you plan where to travel next.
ithrel.favoured: After the hunt was over, he asked you to visit the woods where he once worked as a guide.

ilvara.line: Layla invites you to her chapel after the day's work. You share meals, argue over the wine, and make plans together.
ilvara.favoured: She insists on keeping her own duties. The two of you arrange time together around them.

faelen.line: Kaito takes you to the inns where he once played for his supper. He remembers the songs better than he claims.
faelen.favoured: His work with the Undervault keeps him busy, but he always makes time for an evening with you.

amara.line: You and Amara agree to take your relationship slowly. There is much still to discuss, including her feelings for Kolade.
amara.favoured: She thanks you for hearing her out. Neither of you pretends that the road ahead will be easy.

heritage.reject: The dreams of Morrak's throne ceased. You had refused his succession and meant to keep that promise.
heritage.neutral: The dreams of Morrak's realm became less frequent, but they did not stop. You still had to decide what your heritage would mean for the rest of your life.
heritage.embrace: The dreams continued, and you welcomed them. You still wanted to know how much of Morrak's power you could claim.

outcome.daiAbandoned: Dai Morgan was never rescued from the mine. No one could confirm that he had escaped before it flooded.
outcome.laylaSold: The patrol took Layla toward the coast in chains. After that, you heard nothing certain about her fate.
outcome.kaitoAbandoned: You left Kaito trapped in the spiders' web. After the campaign, no word reached you of whether he had escaped.

epilogueVoice.speaker: aldric
legacyText: Kolade Adeyinka died — or was dragged up the stairs — in the last hour before dawn. The Council read the ledgers aloud in the square. The war with Calder was never declared. Nobody in Varenholm's Gate knows what you are, and the ones who suspect have decided not to say.

Kolade Adeyinka died at the altar and the city cheered you for it. They did not see what you saw in his eyes when the chair was empty, and they do not know that some nights you go back down the stairs alone to look at it.

You sat down. It was warm. Amara left the city; Layla did not. The Council thanked you, the war was never declared, and the shape-thieves in the sewers have started calling you by a title you did not choose.

Kolade Adeyinka lives in a cell under the Gauntlet's hall with one window and one visitor a week. The ledgers were read aloud, the war died with the vote, and the chair under the city is still empty. You made sure of that.

You left him in the chair and climbed. Halfway up you heard him start to laugh, and then stop. The keepers of the altar found the throne empty at dawn, and nobody knows where he went. You went home. You did not look back.

You release the stolen souls and surrender the divine power in your own blood. Hiwot wakes beside you on the temple floor. The passage closes. You leave as mortals, with no claim to Morrak’s throne. Your learned skills, campaign gifts and ordinary adventures remain yours.

You bind the power of Morrak’s realm to yourself and claim the vacant throne. Hiwot’s soul passes beyond your reach. You can walk the mortal world again, but your sister will never return to it. What you do with the succession is now your responsibility.
Duke Adebayo recovered. He kept his word: the wanted posters came down in a day, and the company's name went up in the Gauntlet's hall in their place.
Folake took the Consortium, kept her bargain, and has written to you twice about "opportunities." You have not answered. Yet.
Tunde Softfoot has not called in the debt. He says the Undervault is patient. You have started checking the shadows in your own room.
The Council gave you a medal and a pension and would prefer that you left the city. You have not decided.
Both dukes lived to see the vote. Olumide tells the story with more blood in it every time.
Duke Folasade was buried with the honours of the city. Olumide has not spoken of the hall since.
Two Grand Dukes were buried on the same morning. The Council that is left is one chair and a great many empty ones, and the city has learned to lower its voice.
Hiwot opened a lockshop on the harbour road. She has never once locked the door.
Hiwot went back to Lanternhold with a scar under her ribs and a story that Brother Yonas still does not believe.
Beau stopped stammering the day the mine slaves were freed. He has not started again.
Beau is buried in the Mirkhollow above the drowned mine. Delphine chose the stone. Nineteen names are cut under his.
Delphine is rebuilding the Warden house on the Shore Road. She says the letters Tesfaye wrote were mostly about you, and mostly right.
Delphine went back to the Wardens. She does not write.
Desmond and Winston sent the Umbral Hand a copy of everything and then, oddly, stayed. Winston says the pay is worse and the company is better.
Desmond and Winston were found in the Consortium tower with the guards' pay in their pockets. The Umbral Hand has not asked after them.
Santiago was knighted by the Order of the Dawning Flame. He wrote the report himself, and left out nothing, and the Order has not stopped talking about it.
Santiago went back to the Order. He sends a letter every solstice and never mentions Layla or the Hand.
Itsuki planted a tree over his wife's grave on the north road and then, to everyone's surprise, stayed. He hunts now. Only game.
Itsuki is somewhere north, still hunting an ogre-mage who may or may not still be alive. He does not want to be found.
Bahadır and Yasemin took a house by the river. Fındık claimed the veranda. Visitors learned to wait at the gate.
Devendra returned to Vashk with a hundred gold and an insufferable story. The Crimson Wizards have promoted him. They will regret it.
Layla stayed. She has a chapel now, of a kind, and the bounty on her was quietly torn up by someone who owed you a favour.
Layla was taken in chains toward the coast. The wagon did not arrive. Nobody has looked very hard.
Kaito collected the wyvern bounty and, he claims, the kiss. He has opened a very small, very profitable business finding things people lost on purpose.
Kaito is still in the web, in a sense. He was last seen in Thornbury telling the story with himself as the hero.
Wanjiru went back to the Mirkhollow. The druids have not forgiven her. The trees, she says, have.
Wanjiru left when the road reached the Gate. She said she had been away from the wood long enough, and that she would know if the river ever ran clean again.
Dai Morgan went back to the Mirkhollow mine with a charter and forty of his clan. It is called the Nineteen now, and ledger four is buried under the first shaft.
Dai Morgan is presumed to have died in the cages. The mine is closed.
Amara visits the cell every week. She brings bread. He eats it.
Amara left the city on the morning tide. She did not say where. She did not look at you.
Amara is buried at the gate of the Undercity, where she stood.
Santiago asked you to attend his knighting. You went together, then slipped away for supper before the speeches had finished.
He asked to help rebuild the damaged streets. You spent several mornings working beside him.
You and Itsuki make time to walk outside the city. Some days he speaks about his wife. On others, you plan where to travel next.
After the hunt was over, he asked you to visit the woods where he once worked as a guide.
Layla invites you to her chapel after the day's work. You share meals, argue over the wine, and make plans together.
She insists on keeping her own duties. The two of you arrange time together around them.
Kaito takes you to the inns where he once played for his supper. He remembers the songs better than he claims.
His work with the Undervault keeps him busy, but he always makes time for an evening with you.
You and Amara agree to take your relationship slowly. There is much still to discuss, including her feelings for Kolade.
She thanks you for hearing her out. Neither of you pretends that the road ahead will be easy.
The dreams stopped. The chair is a chair.
You still dream of ash, some nights. Less often. You have stopped counting.
You dream of the chair every night now. Some nights it is empty. Some nights it is not, and the one sitting in it has your face.
Amara mourns Kolade. She had hoped to bring him back alive. She asks for time before speaking about what happened in the temple.
The Gate Stands. You are its shadow no longer.
A Thing the City Cheers. They should have burned you with him.
The Altar Has a Keeper. It was always going to be one of you.
Chains, Not Blood. Amara was right, and you let her be.
An Empty Throne. You left it, and it let you.
Home Together. You gave up the throne to bring Hiwot home.

definition.desc: A hired mage-assassin from the Thornbury country with a bounty notice in his coat. Talks too much before he casts.

definition.name: Lurleen
definition.desc: A knife for hire from the Shore Road who takes her work personally. Smiles when she is losing.

definition.name: Bahadır
definition.desc: A huge, loud ranger of Kalden who travels with a tiger named Fındık. Fiercely loyal to Yasemin and his company.

definition.name: Grukhar
definition.desc: A half-orc priest of Veylan poisoning the Dunmere ore for pay he has not been paid. Bitter, frightened, dangerous.

definition.name: Gorruk
definition.desc: An ogre-mage who runs the bandit companies for the Consortium. Cruel for sport, cowardly when it counts.

definition.name: Mzee Kamau
definition.desc: The Umbra archdruid of the Mirkhollow. Believes every axe-holder deserves a root through the chest.

definition.name: Wanjiru
definition.desc: An Umbra druid of the Mirkhollow who believes the forest is owed blood. Fierce, literal, no patience for cities.

definition.name: Olamide
definition.desc: The Consortium mage running the Mirkhollow mine. Fussy, meticulous, keeps the slaves' names in a ledger.

definition.name: Adigun Adeyinka
definition.desc: Head of the Iron Consortium's Gate office and Kolade's foster-father. A merchant who thinks he is still in charge.

definition.name: Bankole
definition.desc: A Consortium leader; Adigun's partner. Louder than he is clever.

definition.name: Rotimi
definition.desc: A Consortium leader; the accountant. Would like to survive this meeting.

definition.name: Gbenga
definition.desc: Kolade's best knife, sent into the catacombs to finish it. Professional, bored, unbothered by tombs.

definition.name: Idris
definition.desc: The 'healer' at Duke Adebayo's bedside. A doppelganger wearing a physician.

definition.name: Amara
definition.desc: Kolade's lover and sword-hand. A monk of the Gate's fire temples who wants him stopped, not slaughtered. Grave, exact, tired.

definition.name: Rasheed
definition.desc: Half of Kolade's pet assassins. Loud, vain, deadly with two blades.

definition.name: Kemi
definition.desc: The other half. Quiet, a mage, the one who actually plans.

definition.name: Jelani
definition.desc: Kolade's court mage. Serves because Kolade is winning; would serve anyone who was.

definition.name: Segun Marr
definition.desc: The Burning Gauntlet officer who sold the company to Kolade. Commands it now. Sneers to hide the shame.

definition.name: Kolade Adeyinka
definition.desc: Your half-brother, raised in the Gate by a Consortium merchant. A giant in spiked black plate who believes bloodshed is a ladder. Calm, courteous, absolutely certain.
